content.text: Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.309/7bc2d5165d4fffbb7c8d3b5e3b23203c/artifact-capabilities # Artifact runtime capabilities A published Artifact page can declare **runtime capabilities** — abilities the claude.ai viewer grants the page at open time — by passing `capabilities: {name: config}` to the Artifact tool. The control plane is the authority on valid names and config shapes. Declaration gestures: **omitting** `capabilities` on a redeploy carries the stored declaration forward unchanged (and preserves the artifact's stored contract pin); an **empty object** `{}` is the explicit clear-all; a **non-empty object** is a full-set declaration (anything stored but not restated is revoked). Moving a republished artifact's runtime version is a deliberate gesture — pass `contract: 'latest'` to upgrade, or a specific version to pin or roll back — never a side effect of editing. **A page that republishes itself** through the `artifact` capability sends its whole document in exactly the shape the Artifact tool publishes, so a later publish from the tool recognizes and replaces the skeleton instead of nesting it: `` — no whitespace between those tags and nothing else in the head — then the page content exactly as it was written for the tool (its `` and `<style>` first, inside the body, regenerated from the page's state), then `</body></html>`. **Available capabilities:** `artifact`, `assets`, `comments`, `db`, `downloads`, `files`, `mcp`, `room`, `sample`, `self`, `user` — the complete set of capability names you may declare; built in on every page, called without declaring (never pass these in `capabilities`): `permissions`. Anything not listed is unavailable to this user. > Tool spelling in this session: the `Artifact` tool's `action: "read_db"` / `"write_db"` with a `db_op` are the `ArtifactData` tool, whose `action` is that `db_op` ("get", "list", "query", "set", "update", "str_replace", "delete", "batch") with the other fields unchanged — load it with ToolSearch when you first need it. Read the steps below with that substitution. Runtime contract 0.2.94 Capability namespaces live behind `claude.use(name)`: `const db = await claude.use("db")` resolves the capability's namespace, or `null` when this view cannot run it (not served, not granted, or failed to load — indistinguishable by design). Branch on `null` and design for absence. `window.claude` carries only `use`: no `window.claude.db`, `.room`, or `.artifact` member is ever promised, so never read one — render the page without them and light features up when the promise resolves (later, never within your script's first run, and unordered with DOMContentLoaded; `null` after 10 s when no viewer answers). The resolved namespace is frozen and platform-owned: call its functions and keep the reference; never assign to it, `defineProperty` on it, or replace a member (wrap it for your own helpers). Permission stays on the calls: a consent prompt, rate limit, or policy refusal arrives on the first call, never from `use()`. Awaiting `use("db")` again is free (memoized); an unknown name resolves `null`. --- capability: artifact --- Use `artifact` for pages that should remember what people do with them: polls, sign-up sheets, checklists, trackers, boards — the page is the record; data kept server-side, or seeded or read back by Claude, is `db`. Declare `capabilities: {artifact: {}}`; `const artifact = await claude.use("artifact")`, then `await artifact.publish(html)` saves `html` (a complete document, doctype first) as the new version, and every open view, this one included, reloads to it. Nothing a viewer types, ticks or drags is kept unless the page publishes it. So embed the shared state as data in the HTML you publish and render the page from it; when an interaction completes, update the state, regenerate the document and publish it — never serialize the live DOM; batch rapid edits into one publish; publish only after a viewer acts, never on load. `conflict` is routine (every view reloads to the winner, dropping this edit): no retry. For read-only viewers publish rejects `not_granted`/`not_writer` — render a read-only view. --- capability: assets --- `assets` stores uploaded assets: `const assets = await claude.use("assets")`; `assets.upload(blob)` (image, SVG, video, PDF, font, CSS/JS, or CSV/Markdown/JSON/text; 20 MiB cap, CSS/JS 16 MiB, SVG 2 MiB and sanitized) resolves `{id, url, sizeBytes, contentType}`; `assets.list()` resolves `{assets, usage}`; `assets.delete(id)` removes one for good: only on a deliberate user action, updating rows that held it. Declare `capabilities: {assets: {}}`: only Editors and up get it, others get `null` from `use("assets")` (hide asset UI; handle errors). Only if the user wants uploads from non-editors, declare `{assets: {upload: "interact"}}`: where enabled, Contributors can upload but list and delete only their own, and their files show only in the organization; never run any asset as code, CSS or HTML. Store the `id` in `db` rows as the durable pointer; use the returned `url` as an `<img>`/`<video>`/`<a>` source (SVG: `<img>` or CSS only); a stored id serves at `"/_blob/" + id`. The type definitions are authoritative. --- capability: comments --- `comments` wires a page's own commenting UI to the artifact's shared comment store: `await claude.use("comments")` (`null`: unavailable). The declaration picks the grant: `capabilities: {comments: {"composer_only": true}}` grants only `openComposer({element}|{range})` (opens the shell's composer like a comment-mode click; prefer it for discoverable entry points) and `anchorFor`, no consent asked. The full form `{comments: {}}` adds write verbs acting as the viewer under consent; public-link visitors and email invitees get `null`. `"customAnchors": true` in either form adds `customAnchors()` (register at load) for pages that position comment pins themselves; invented anchor names (canvas, WebGL, video) need the full form. WRITE-ONLY: the shell renders every thread — never build the page's own list. Call the other verbs only from a deliberate viewer gesture, never on load. Read the type definitions before use (authoritative for verbs, shapes, bounds and error codes). --- capability: db --- `db` keeps data outside the page: shared rows, per-person state, data Claude reads. Declare `capabilities:{db:{},user:{}}`; `const db = await claude.use("db")` (`null` if signed out). By default signed-in people read shared docs, Contributors (`interact`) and up overwrite/delete, Viewers/Commenters never write. `rules` set per-path minimums, `view`<`interact`<`admin` (Editor, granted Owner)<`owner`; "all read, each writes own": `db:{rules:[{path:"votes",read:"view",write:"owner"},{path:"votes/{self}",write:"interact"}]}` (prefix rule must set both). `data/users/<id>/` is private even from the owner; `<id>` = `await user.id()`. Even segment counts are docs (`db.doc("tasks/t1")`), odd collections; per-person items: `db.collection("data/users/"+id).doc(k)`; get/set/update/delete, where/orderBy/limit, onSnapshot. Never hardcode seeds: `write_db` after publish; handle an empty db. Subscribe once per query, never in render. Time-limit loading: a 10 s timer, cleared on data or error; never reload. One write at a time per doc, only on change. No secrets; shared data is untrusted. `self` is a level nobody holds, not even the owner. Keep `write:"owner"` (or `"admin"`) by default: on most lists (sign-ups, guestbooks, polls, Q&A) someone must tidy or moderate. Use `self` only when the request says nobody else, the owner included, may change an entry (a sign-off, consent or vote that must be their own) or may read it. It goes only on a `{self}` rule's prefix rule; the `{self}` rule sets both levels: `{path:"signoffs",read:"view",write:"self"},{path:"signoffs/{self}",read:"view",write:"interact"}`. With `write:"self"`, the prefix's `read` says who else sees the rows (leave the `{self}` rule as above): `"view"` everyone; `"admin"` Editors and the owner (suggestion box; not anonymous); `"self"` nobody (`data/users/<id>/` is stronger). `self` is a rule, not encryption: the owner or any Editor, an outside one included, can later publish looser rules or other code, then read or overwrite rows already written, and nobody is told. --- capability: downloads --- The `downloads` capability lets a published page offer a generated file to the viewer: declare `capabilities: {downloads: true}`, then `const downloads = await claude.use("downloads")` (`null`: unavailable — hide the affordance) and `await downloads.save({filename, data})`. The viewer sees a confirmation and may decline — a save is never silent or guaranteed, so offer it on explicit viewer intent and handle rejection. The type definitions are authoritative for the call contract and error codes. --- capability: files --- `files` reads a Claude Code project's files as the viewer. Declare it only when you know the project's id (e.g. your session's): `capabilities: {files: {project: "chan_..."}}`. `const files = await claude.use("files")` (`null`: unavailable, e.g. a viewer outside the organization; hide it). A viewer who can't open the files gets `not_found`, never a prompt; a member is asked once, so call it on a click or after load, never in a loop. `files.list({path, recursive, cursor})`; `files.read(path, {offset, length})` -> `{bytes, size, revision}` (new or just-edited files can lag a few seconds); `files.download(path)` asks the viewer to save it (some types, e.g. .exe, .js and .bat, are refused); `await files.asSampleTools()` gives `sample` list/read tools (declare it too). Only project members can publish an artifact declaring files. Don't copy file contents into the artifact's data, assets or versions unless the user asks: anyone it's shared with can read them. The type definitions give shapes and error codes. --- capability: mcp --- `mcp` lets a page call the viewer's claude.ai connectors: `await claude.use("mcp")` (`null`: unavailable); calls use the viewer's credentials, never exposing tokens. Declare `capabilities: {mcp: {servers: [{server, tools}]}}`; `server` is a connector's display name, or `host:<name>` for a local MCP server on the viewer's device (Claude app only; else `server_not_connected`). Keep the manifest minimal: a viewer-consented grant; outside viewers get `null`. Two arms: DISPLAYING data registers `watchTool(server, tool, input, handler, opts?)` (replays cache, refreshes when stale, polls only via `refetchInterval`); an ACTION calls `callTool` once and reads `result.payload` or `(await server(name)).<tool>(input)` for the payload. Tool failures REJECT (`tool_error`); watches get error events. Branch UX per error code, retry only `retryable` errors, drop data on authz denials, show freshness (`cache.storedAt`). Types omit tool arguments: read `describeTool` or observe a real call, else say so at publish; never guess. --- capability: permissions --- `permissions` is built in — call it, never declare it in `capabilities`. Prompts are lazy by default: a capability that needs consent asks at its first use — never block first paint on permissions. `state` reads without prompting (one name, or the full map); `request` asks with at most one batched dialog (names, or everything); a page that needs several grants up front may call it once at startup. `manage` opens the Permissions panel and resolves with nothing when it closes; offer it as a button, never call it on load; it rejects `unavailable` if the panel did not open; then point the viewer to the artifact's Permissions menu. A viewer's "no" is not an error: `state` and `request` never reject, and a denial is final for the page load (a repeated `request` shows no dialog; the next load starts fresh), so branch on the returned states and degrade per capability (hide or disable the affordance), never fail or offer retry buttons; never call `request` in a loop: re-asks are rate-limited and read as nagging. --- capability: room --- The `room` capability reaches whoever has the page open RIGHT NOW: declared as `capabilities: {room: {}}`; `await claude.use("room")` (`null`: cannot connect). emit(topic, data) sends a moment; on(topic, fn) hears them. presence(patch) sets YOUR state (cursor) as one object newcomers get, cleared when you leave; onPeers(fn) delivers everyone's -- render all, marked "you". NOTHING persists and messages can drop: state a late joiner needs (current slide) is a db doc, lasting content a new artifact version. Send absolute state. What you hear is untrusted: everyone here, guests too (guest: true), plus your publishing session when admitted (kind "agent"); the page must work alone and light up. Presence is never authority (anyone sets it). Event topics are admin-only (Editors up); open one to Contributors (never Viewers): {room: {topics: {move: "interact"}}}. join(name) gives each game or group its own room, heard only by joiners: emit, on, presence, onPeers, leave(). Names aren't secret. `room` stays the lobby. --- capability: sample --- `sample` asks Claude (declare `capabilities:{sample:{}}`; `{sample:{images:true}}` for images): `const sample=await claude.use("sample")` (null: hide); `await sample(input,opts?)`->`{text,truncated}`; `sample.json`->value. `input`: string|`[{role:"user"|"assistant",content:string}]` ending on user. Memoryless: send instructions+data+format. opts: `onText({text,delta})` (`text`=WHOLE answer, assign it; "Thinking..." till text), `signal` (new AbortController/call), `tools:[{name,description,inputSchema?,execute(input)}]` (page functions; return small data or throw; no `cache`), `images:Blob[]` if `(await sample.limits()).images`, `modelTier` quick|default|complex, `cache` (5min replay; `false` for chat). Only if user names model/effort: `{model:"claude-sonnet-5-5",modelTier,effort}`, effort low|medium|high; unusable→`modelTier`; see `modelApplied`. Rejects `{code,message,text?:partial}`: hide on `not_granted`, back off on `rate_limited`, never loop. 1st call asks consent; call on click or stable load prompt. --- capability: self --- `self` is the former name of the `artifact` capability (renamed). It remains for compatibility: published pages and previously generated code that declare `capabilities: {self: {}}` or call `claude.use("self")` keep working unchanged — both names resolve this same capability (this contract promises no `window.claude.self` member to feature-check; `use()` is the check). Do not use it in new pages: declare `capabilities: {artifact: {}}` and obtain the namespace with `await claude.use("artifact")`; see the artifact section for how to use it. --- capability: user --- `user` answers who is viewing this page and who your shared state names: the owner's organization and invited guests (`guest: true`); others are absent. `const user = await claude.use("user")`; `null` = absent (`user?.isOwner() ?? false`). `isOwner()`/`canEdit()`/`can(name)` need no setup (canEdit = admin level; `can("data.write")` = may write shared `db` docs, `null` = not told: keep the input; refused writes decide). Declare `capabilities:{user:{}}` for `id()`/`me()` (opaque id, comparable only within one scope; `me()` never null) and `profiles(ids)`; `scopes:["profile"]` adds names and `search(q)`; `["profile","email"]` adds addresses. Reads never reject. Store only ids (`id()` or `hit.id`), never a name, avatar, or Profile: names differ per viewer and go stale. Resolve in render, every time: `const ps = await user.profiles(idsOnScreen)` then `ps[id].name || 'Someone'` (cached: call again freely). `name` is `""` if unresolvable: use `||` not `??`. Call `search('')` on focus; set names with textContent. **Your connectors this session.** In this session the Claude app has connected the user's claude.ai connectors under opaque ids: their tools appear in your tool list as `mcp__<id>__<toolName>`. The ids belong to these connectors: `18de32a0-663e-4cda-85df-2a68e5916451` is "Microsoft 365"; `1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c` is "Claude Docs"; `20ba8580-bd26-489b-9d1c-034028af6897` is "Admin.News editor desk"; `5e372661-4882-4ca5-aa11-01f32e42148c` is "PostHog"; `67ee3575-9119-4cb7-8271-686e88098cbe` is "Admin.News contributor desk"; `c39b39a8-1877-4f58-88b0-3495605b1158` is "Riverside"; `ca96bd93-49d1-4e81-9bc2-52eebc045846` is "Gmail". For these, set `server` to the connector's name exactly as written here, e.g. `{"server": "Microsoft 365", "tools": [...]}` — never the id or any `mcp__` segment — and in the page pass that same name as the `server` argument of `callTool`/`watchTool`, because viewers resolve connectors by name only. Locally-configured MCP servers connected in this session can also be declared, as host servers: set `server` to `host:<server>` where `<server>` is the segment between `mcp__` and the next `__` in that server's tool names (`mcp__filesystem__read_file` → `host:filesystem`). Only servers from the user's MCP configuration count, with one built-in exception: `host:claude_browser` is the Claude app's own browser — declare it, with the tools the page needs from `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `preview_start`, `navigate`, `computer` and `form_input`, when the page must read or act on other websites; it answers only when the viewer opens the page in the Claude desktop app; the viewer is asked once, at the page's first call to it, and again at each click or key press that calls a banking or other high-risk site. The app's other built-in servers (`cowork`, `scheduled-tasks`, `session_info`, `workspace` and the like) are never host servers, and a page that declares one is refused at publish. The `mcp__<id>__` connectors above are claude.ai connectors, never host servers. A host server only answers when the viewer opens the page in a Claude app that has that same local server connected — say so to the user when you publish. The manifest's `tools` array takes the connector's upstream tool names (as returned by `listTools()`), which can differ from the normalized `<toolName>` segment when an upstream name contains `.` or spaces. 1	/**
2	 * The `db` capability — a persistent, realtime document store for this
3	 * artifact, shared by its viewers.
4	 *
5	 * One store per artifact: JSON documents at slash-separated paths
6	 * (`collection/doc`, nesting deeper as `collection/doc/subcollection/doc`),
7	 * surviving reloads, republishes, and sessions. The store is created on
8	 * the first write and erased when the artifact is deleted. Reads and
9	 * subscriptions see other viewers' writes live. Declare
10	 * `capabilities: {db: {}}`. Only the owner can write, plus anyone invited
11	 * by email as an editor (where the share menu offers that level, and only
12	 * while the artifact is not also shared by a public link), plus,
13	 * on a plan with other members (such as Team or Enterprise), the members
14	 * who can open the artifact, unless their sharing level is view-only
15	 * (`view`). A view-only member can only read shared data, never write it.
16	 * Anyone else is an outside viewer: they never write, and read shared data
17	 * only when signed in, through a public link or an email invitation.
18	 *
19	 * ACCESS RULES. By default everyone admitted reads shared documents,
20	 * those at `interact` or above also write them, and each viewer's own
21	 * `data/users/<id>/` subtree is private.
22	 * To change who may read or write where, declare rules keyed on the
23	 * viewer's sharing level — `interact` (the share menu's Contributor: uses
24	 * the page and changes its shared data), `admin` (the share menu's Editor
25	 * or Owner: also publishes versions and assets; an Editor from outside
26	 * the organization, invited by email, holds it only while the artifact
27	 * is not also shared by link), `owner` (the artifact's own owner; not a
28	 * person granted Owner), plus `view`, the lowest level, for paths that
29	 * should stay readable by everyone the server admits (Viewers, Commenters
30	 * and outside visitors hold `view`; it only ever widens reads, never
31	 * writes) — as the minimum level for each action at a path and below:
32	 *   capabilities: { db: { rules: [
33	 *     { path: "", read: "interact", write: "admin" },
34	 *     { path: "data/users/{self}", write: "interact" },
35	 *   ] } }
36	 * reads "viewers at `interact` or above read shared data, only editors
37	 * write it, and each of them writes their own subtree". A rule applies
38	 * to its path and everything below; a deeper rule overrides it there and
39	 * may be stricter or looser. A level left unset inherits from the nearest
40	 * rule above (the root defaults to read: "view", write: "interact").
41	 * A fifth word, `self`, comes with `{self}` below.
42	 * An artifact created from a type often ships with that type's rules
43	 * already declared (commonly `write: "admin"` on shared data): read its
44	 * manifest before assuming the defaults.
45	 * Inheritance reaches each viewer's own subtree too: with no
46	 * `data/users/{self}` rule declared it inherits like any other path, so
47	 * locking the root alone (`{ path: "", write: "admin" }`) also stops
48	 * everyone below `admin` writing their own subtree. A page where only
49	 * editors change shared data and each person at Contributor or above
50	 * still fills in their own part also declares
51	 * `{ path: "data/users/{self}", write: "interact" }` beside it (each
52	 * part stays hidden from everyone else, the owner and editors included,
53	 * unless a rule at `data/users` opens it, see below). Put data that only
54	 * editors may change under its own path with a raised write level:
55	 *   { path: "data/editors-only", write: "admin" }
56	 * It lets everyone who reads shared data read it and only `admin` and
57	 * above write it, there and below. `data/editors-only` is itself a
58	 * document path, so keep collections below it, as in
59	 * `data/editors-only/notes/n1`. Add `read: "admin"` and it reads as
60	 * non-existent to everyone below `admin`, in `get`, queries and
61	 * `onSnapshot` alike.
62	 * Writing implies reading: a rule's write level is never below its read
63	 * level. A path ending in `/{self}` names each viewer's own subtree under
64	 * that prefix: nobody else — the artifact's owner included — sees a
65	 * sibling's subtree unless a rule at the prefix opens it, and `{self}`
66	 * must be the last segment. `{self}` works under ANY prefix, not only
67	 * `data/users`: "everyone reads the votes, each viewer writes only
68	 * their own" is
69	 *   { path: "votes", read: "view", write: "owner" },
70	 *   { path: "votes/{self}", write: "interact" }
71	 * with each viewer writing `votes/<their id>` (or documents below it)
72	 * and only the owner able to change someone else's; `write: "admin"` on
73	 * the prefix would also let every Editor, and anyone granted Owner, do
74	 * so. A rule declared AT the prefix of a `{self}` rule (here `votes`)
75	 * must set BOTH `read` and `write`, or the declaration is rejected at
76	 * publish; with no prefix rule, siblings' subtrees stay private as under
77	 * `data/users`.
78	 * `self` is a level nobody holds, not even the owner. It goes only on
79	 * the rule AT the prefix of a declared `{self}` rule (here `votes`),
80	 * never on the root or on the `{self}` rule itself. On someone else's
81	 * subtree only the prefix rule applies; on a viewer's own, whichever of
82	 * the two rules gives them more.
83	 * Keep `write: "owner"` or `"admin"` on the prefix by default: on most
84	 * lists (a sign-up sheet, a guestbook, a poll, a Q&A board) somebody must

87	 * may change an entry, or that an entry has to be that person's own act
88	 * (a sign-off, an approval, a consent, a vote nobody may touch), or that
89	 * nobody else may read it:
90	 *   { path: "signoffs", read: "view", write: "self" },
91	 *   { path: "signoffs/{self}", read: "view", write: "interact" }
92	 * With `write: "self"`, choose `read` by who else should see the
93	 * documents:

95	 *                                  each writes only their own
96	 *   read: "admin", write: "self"   a suggestion box: each writes only
97	 *                                  their own, Editors and the owner read
98	 *                                  them all
99	 *   read: "self",  write: "self"   a notebook private from the other
100	 *                                  people on the artifact: nobody else
101	 *                                  reads or writes it

103	 * count wants the suggestion box's pattern, whose readers see who chose
104	 * what, or Hidden-until-reveal below. `read: "self"` is valid only with
105	 * `write: "self"`. Beside a prefix rule that uses `self`, state both
106	 * levels on the `{self}` rule, as above: they set who writes their own
107	 * subtree, and who reads it where the prefix's `read` does not already
108	 * admit them.
109	 * A viewer who can read only their own `{self}` subtree (a Contributor
110	 * in the suggestion box, anyone in the notebook) gets just their own
111	 * documents from a listener or query on the prefix collection.
112	 * `self` is a rule, not encryption. It stops only other people's direct
113	 * reads and writes: paths and ids are stored in the clear, page code runs
114	 * as whoever is viewing, and the owner or any Editor (whoever can publish
115	 * the artifact or its type, an Editor from outside the organization
116	 * included) can later publish looser rules or other code, then read or
117	 * overwrite the documents already stored. Nobody is told. Before loosening
118	 * a `self` rule, tell whoever asked what it would expose. While
119	 * `write: "self"` stands, nobody else can correct or remove one viewer's
120	 * documents, short of deleting the artifact. For data kept from everyone

122	 * loosening-proof: unless a version declared a rule at `data/users`, or
123	 * at `data` beside `data/{self}`, nobody else has ever reached it.
124	 * At most 64 rules; paths follow the
125	 * document-path grammar below. The owner meets every level but `self`,
126	 * so only `self` and `{self}` privacy limit the owner. Who holds
127	 * which level, in the share menu's words (Owner, Editor, Contributor,
128	 * Commenter, Viewer): Editor and Owner hold `admin`; an Editor from
129	 * outside the organization, invited by email (where the menu offers
130	 * that), holds it unless the artifact is also shared by link. A person
131	 * granted Owner in the share menu holds `admin`, not `owner`, and so do
132	 * the members who can post in an added channel or project granted it:
133	 * `owner` is only the artifact's own owner (`isOwner()`). On an artifact
134	 * a person owns, that is one person; on an artifact Claude made in a
135	 * channel or project, it is the members of that channel or project who
136	 * can post in it. The share menu shows the artifact's own owner (that
137	 * person, or that channel or project) first in its list of who has
138	 * access, in a row that cannot be changed or removed, whatever level
139	 * name that row shows.
140	 * Contributor, on a person or on general access, holds `interact`, as
141	 * does a member of the organization who arrives by a public link. Viewer
142	 * and Commenter hold `view`, as does every signed-in visitor from
143	 * outside the organization, by public link or email invitation, except
144	 * the outside Editor above while the artifact is not shared by link. On
145	 * an artifact a person owns, a member whom general access also admits
146	 * (organization-wide, or by a public link) holds the higher of their own
147	 * level and the level it gives, so being listed as Viewer or Commenter
148	 * does not lower them. A person who stays at Commenter under that rule
149	 * reads and comments and writes no data, their own `data/users/<id>/`
150	 * subtree included. A signed-out visitor has no data at all. So by
151	 * default only `interact` and above write shared documents or their own
152	 * subtree, and a page where each person saves their own data needs them
153	 * at Contributor or above. A call below the minimum fails the same way
154	 * as a sibling's `{self}` subtree: a read sees a non-existent document
155	 * and a write rejects `invalid_argument` —
156	 * so gate controls up front on what the `user` capability reports
157	 * (`can("data.write")` = may write shared documents under the root rule;
158	 * `canEdit()` = admin, for controls a rule reserves for admin;
159	 * `isOwner()` = owner) rather than branching on the code. When

171	 * it resolves `null` when this view cannot run db (not served, not

177	/** Rejection shape for every method and the `onSnapshot` error
178	 * callback. `message` is human-readable but not localized. */
179	type DbError = {
180	  code: DbErrorCode;
181	  message: string;
182	};
183	
184	/**
185	 * Stable error codes. Branch on `code`, never on message text; treat
186	 * unknown codes as `"unavailable"`.
187	 *
188	 * Store codes — the complete set for store operations:
189	 * - `invalid_argument` — the path, body, or query breaks a rule in
190	 *   the docs below (bad path grammar, non-object body, a document
191	 *   over 256 KiB or 32 levels deep, too many filters, an
192	 *   over-limit page size, ...). Surfaces at call time for verbs
193	 *   and on the error callback at subscribe time. Fix the call;
194	 *   retrying cannot succeed.
195	 * - `resource_exhausted` — a budget: the per-viewer call rate, the
196	 *   subscription cap (64 per view), too many concurrent writes or
197	 *   active leases, or a query that scans too many documents. Slow
198	 *   down, subscribe to less, or narrow the query; tightening a loop
199	 *   on it cannot succeed.
200	 * - `quota_exceeded` — a cap is full: documents in the collection,
201	 *   documents in this artifact's database, the organization's
202	 *   databases, or the total size of this artifact's database (the
203	 *   message names which). Not transient: at a count cap creating
204	 *   documents fails until some are deleted, while writes to existing
205	 *   documents still succeed; at the size cap creating documents can
206	 *   fail, and so can a write that makes an existing document larger,
207	 *   until documents are deleted or made smaller. Surface it to the
208	 *   viewer; retrying cannot succeed.
209	 * - `unavailable` — a transient platform condition. Verbs: retry
210	 *   once after a short randomized delay. Subscriptions handle this
211	 *   INTERNALLY and in silence (see `onSnapshot`): an error callback
212	 *   never receives it, EXCEPT when the page's host itself stops
213	 *   answering: that listener is terminated with `unavailable` and a
214	 *   fresh `onSnapshot` is the only recovery.
215	 * - `revoked` — this view's grant was withdrawn while the page was
216	 *   running (access, sharing, or availability changed). Terminal for
217	 *   the page load: at most one delivery per listener; calls reject
218	 *   thereafter. Render the degraded experience; don't editorialize
219	 *   about why — the surrounding app owns access messaging.
220	 *
221	 * There is deliberately NO `permission-denied` and NO not-found code
222	 * on reads: a document this viewer cannot see behaves exactly like
223	 * one that does not exist (`exists: false`, omitted from queries).
224	 *
225	 * Lifecycle codes (from the runtime itself, not the store):
226	 * - `not_granted` — this view did not grant db to the frame.
227	 * - `capability_disabled` — granted but not usable in this view
228	 *   (the serving runtime predates it or its module failed to load).
229	 * - `capability_removed` — the called method is not part of the
230	 *   runtime serving this view; treat like `capability_disabled`.
231	 * - `transform_error` — the call's arguments could not be prepared;
232	 *   treat like `invalid_argument`.
233	 * (`queue_overflow`, from runtimes that queue calls made before they
234	 * are ready, can also reach an error callback; it is terminal for that
235	 * listener and falls under the unknown-code rule above.)
236	 */
237	type DbErrorCode =
238	  | "invalid_argument"
239	  | "resource_exhausted"
240	  | "quota_exceeded"
241	  | "unavailable"
242	  | "revoked"
243	  | "not_granted"
244	  | "capability_disabled"
245	  | "capability_removed"
246	  | "transform_error";
247	
248	/**
249	 * PATH GRAMMAR (shared by every ref). A document path has an EVEN
250	 * number of slash-separated segments — the last is the document id,
251	 * the joined rest is its collection (`tasks/t1`, or nested:
252	 * `boards/b1/columns/c2`). A collection path is the odd-length
253	 * prefix form (`tasks`, `boards/b1/columns`). Count segments before
254	 * choosing the builder. `data/users/<id>` (3) is a COLLECTION — the
255	 * viewer's own — so one document per viewer is
256	 * `db.doc("data/users/" + uid + "/profile")` (4), and one document per
257	 * deck is `db.collection("data/users/" + uid).doc(deckId)` (4).
258	 * `data/users/<id>/decks` (4) is therefore a DOCUMENT path, not a
259	 * collection: a named per-viewer list is a subcollection under a
260	 * per-viewer document,
261	 * `db.doc("data/users/" + uid + "/profile").collection("decks")` (5),
262	 * each deck `.doc(deckId)` below it (6) — building from a ref like
263	 * this keeps the parity right for you. Segments use letters, digits,
264	 * and `_ - . ~ : @ +` only (never `.` or `..` alone); at most
265	 * 200 bytes per segment, 1000 bytes and 16 segments per path.
266	 * `doc()`, `collection()` and the builders on refs THROW a
267	 * `TypeError` synchronously for a path that breaks
268	 * this grammar (its message names the broken rule; for parity, the
269	 * segment count) — a programming error to fix where the path is
270	 * written, not a store condition to handle; building a ref never
271	 * touches the network. Paths are data you choose — there is no need to
272	 * pre-create a collection, and deleting a document does NOT delete
273	 * documents nested under its path.
274	 *
275	 * The `data/users/` path prefix is special, platform-side: each
276	 * viewer's own subtree under it is private per viewer — including
277	 * from the artifact's owner (the default `data/users/{self}` rule;
278	 * a declared rule at the `data/users` prefix opens siblings' subtrees
279	 * at its levels, see ACCESS RULES above). Address the viewer's subtree as
280	 * `data/users/<id>/...` using the AWAITED value of
281	 * {@link Claude.user.id} (declare `user` alongside `db` — without
282	 * the declaration `id()` resolves null; it is async, and an
283	 * un-awaited promise is not a valid path segment, so the builder
284	 * throws) — the
285	 * store recognizes exactly that id as this viewer, no other value
286	 * works. A null id means no private subtree: disable the per-viewer
287	 * feature for that visit rather than relocating its data to a
288	 * shared path; a view-only or comment-only member has an id yet cannot
289	 * write there either, so treat a rejected write the same way. Another
290	 * viewer's documents under `data/users/`
291	 * read as non-existent (`exists: false`, omitted from queries and
292	 * `onSnapshot`) — the "shared by its viewers" default does NOT
293	 * apply inside this prefix — and a write (`set`/`update`/`delete`)
294	 * into another viewer's subtree rejects `invalid_argument`.
295	 * Hidden-until-reveal (sealed votes, planning poker): each viewer
296	 * writes their pick under their own `data/users/<id>/` path, where by
297	 * default nobody else can read it, and copies it to a shared path when
298	 * THEY reveal — rules are fixed at publish, so nothing a page does at
299	 * run time opens another viewer's subtree.
300	 */
301	
302	/** Snapshot provenance. `fromCache: true` marks a view the store has
303	 * not confirmed, such as a copy saved on an earlier visit, your own
304	 * writes before the first read lands, a collection too large to read
305	 * whole, or delivery during a connectivity gap. A definitive snapshot
306	 * follows by itself once the store answers in full.
307	 * `hasPendingWrites` is true while the view includes this page's own
308	 * unconfirmed write (latency compensation). */
309	type SnapshotMetadata = {
310	  fromCache: boolean;
311	  hasPendingWrites: boolean;
312	};
313	
314	/** One document, as reads and snapshots deliver it. Delivered
315	 *  snapshots and their `data()` are frozen; a document that didn't
316	 *  change is the same object across deliveries — compare with
317	 *  `===`, don't mutate or accumulate them (clone a body before
318	 *  editing it for a write). */
319	type DocumentSnapshot = {
320	  /** The last segment of the document's path. */
321	  id: string;
322	  /** False covers both a missing document and one this viewer cannot
323	   * see — deliberately indistinguishable. */
324	  exists: boolean;
325	  /** The document body; `undefined` when `exists` is false. */
326	  data(): Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
327	  metadata: SnapshotMetadata;
328	};
329	
330	/** One ordered-view transition inside a query snapshot. Indexes are
331	 * positions in the snapshot's `docs` order: `oldIndex` is -1 for
332	 * `added`, `newIndex` is -1 for `removed`. `removed` covers
333	 * deletion, leaving the query, and losing visibility, identically; its
334	 * `doc` is the last snapshot the listener saw (`exists: true`,
335	 * carrying the final body), so a removal handler still has the data. */
336	type DocumentChange = {
337	  type: "added" | "modified" | "removed";
338	  doc: DocumentSnapshot;
339	  oldIndex: number;
340	  newIndex: number;
341	};
342	
343	/** A query's matched set, in query order. */
344	type QuerySnapshot = {
345	  docs: DocumentSnapshot[];
346	  size: number;
347	  empty: boolean;
348	  /** The changes since the previous snapshot of this listener (the
349	   * first snapshot is all-`added`). */
350	  docChanges(): DocumentChange[];
351	  metadata: SnapshotMetadata;
352	};
353	
354	/** Stop receiving snapshots. Idempotent; after it returns, the
355	 * callbacks never fire again. */
356	type Unsubscribe = () => void;
357	
358	type AcquireOptions = {
359	  /** Who holds the lease — any stable string (a viewer id, a tab
360	   * id). Renewal requires the same holder. */
361	  holder: string;
362	  /** Requested lease length in milliseconds. Absent/0 means 30000;
363	   * values are clamped to [1000, 600000], never rejected. */
364	  ttlMs?: number;
365	  /** Merged into the document body when the lease is granted. */
366	  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
367	};
368	
369	type AcquireResult = {
370	  acquired: boolean;
371	  /** The document's version after a granted acquire. */
372	  version?: number;
373	  /** RFC 3339 expiry of the lease now in force (granted or not). */
374	  expiresAt?: string;
375	  /** Your own holder string, echoed on a granted acquire; absent when
376	   * busy — the platform reveals `expiresAt`, never who holds it. */
377	  holder?: string;
378	};
379	
380	/**
381	 * A reference to one document. Pure and synchronous to create — a
382	 * malformed path throws here; nothing reaches the store until a
383	 * terminal call.
384	 */
385	type DocumentReference = {
386	  /** The last path segment. */
387	  id: string;
388	  path: string;
389	
390	  /** Read once. Absence is NOT an error — branch on `exists`. */
391	  get(): Promise<DocumentSnapshot>;
392	
393	  /** Write the WHOLE document, creating it (and the store) if
394	   * absent — a full replace, Firestore-style. Use `update` to merge
395	   * into existing fields. Writes are last-writer-wins; there are no
396	   * transactions.
397	   *
398	   * ONE WRITE AT A TIME per document, only when its data changed:
399	   * await each `set`/`update` before the next to the same document;
400	   * write on a user action or a real state change, never from render
401	   * code, a snapshot callback, or a timer that rewrites unchanged or
402	   * clock-derived values; coalesce a burst of input events into one
403	   * write per pause. The page open in other tabs or devices writes the
404	   * same documents; overlapping writes to one document make each write
405	   * slower. */
406	  set(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>;
407	
408	  /** Merge-write that REQUIRES the document to exist — rejects
409	   * `invalid_argument` otherwise (creating-on-miss would be a bug
410	   * for its use cases). Nested objects merge recursively; anything
411	   * else (arrays included) replaces that field wholesale. Same
412	   * one-write-at-a-time rule as `set`. Do NOT build monotonic
413	   * counters from read-modify-update — writes are last-writer-wins
414	   * and a retried write can apply twice. */
415	  update(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>;
416	
417	  /** Delete this document. Idempotent; nested documents survive. */
418	  delete(): Promise<void>;
419	
420	  /**
421	   * Cooperative short lease on this document — set-if-not-busy, the
422	   * single-writer primitive (one editor at a time, a migration that
423	   * should run once, a turn lock). NOT a security boundary: other
424	   * viewers can still write directly; leases only coordinate
425	   * callers that all use `acquire`. Busy resolves
426	   * `{acquired: false}` — a normal outcome, never an error. Leases
427	   * expire on their own (no release verb): prefer short `ttlMs`
428	   * and renew while working. There is no create-if-absent write, so
429	   * "claim a slot" (a seat, a username, first-come ownership) is:
430	   * `acquire` the slot document (short `ttlMs`, no `data`), `get()`
431	   * it, and while you hold the lease `set` your claim only if it does
432	   * not exist yet or its body names no owner, then let the lease
433	   * lapse; `{acquired: false}` means someone else is mid-claim — treat
434	   * the slot as taken or re-read after `expiresAt`. Do not carry the
435	   * claim in `acquire`'s `data` (it merges on every later grant too).
436	   * A bare get-then-set races and both callers believe they won.
437	   */
438	  acquire(options: AcquireOptions): Promise<AcquireResult>;
439	
440	  /**
441	   * Subscribe to this document. `next` fires with the current state
442	   * once the store answers, then on every change — including other
443	   * viewers' writes, live. Your own writes appear immediately
444	   * (`hasPendingWrites: true` until confirmed), and a returning viewer
445	   * may first get a copy saved on an earlier visit (`fromCache: true`).
446	   * Delivery rides a realtime stream when available and falls back to
447	   * periodic refresh (about 30 s foreground) — same callbacks either way.
448	   * While the store cannot be reached (offline, or a network that
449	   * holds, drops or blocks its requests) the listener may hear nothing
450	   * from it, not even an error, and keeps retrying until it answers.
451	   * So time-limit loading: start a timer of about 10 s when you
452	   * subscribe. If it fires, say the data can't be reached yet or, over
453	   * anything already delivered, that it may be out of date. The first
454	   * snapshot with `fromCache: false` clears the timer and that note; so
455	   * does `error`, which ends the loading state too. Until `error` fires,
456	   * keep the listener: never reload the page or subscribe again to
457	   * recover.
458	   * `error` receives at most one terminal {@link DbError}
459	   * (`invalid_argument`, `resource_exhausted`, `revoked`, or the
460	   * `unavailable` above), after which the subscription
461	   * is dead. Pass it: without one a terminal error is reported via
462	   * `reportError` (your `error` event and console see it) and the
463	   * listener still dies.
464	   *
465	   * SUBSCRIBE ONCE per document or query (when the view starts, or
466	   * when the path or filter really changes), keep the returned
467	   * `Unsubscribe`, and call it when done. Never subscribe from code
468	   * that runs on every render (a React component body, a `render()`
469	   * function, anything the snapshot callback triggers): each call
470	   * opens another subscription, each snapshot re-renders, and the
471	   * page loops. In React, subscribe in a `useEffect`, build the ref or
472	   * query inside it, depend only on stable primitives, and return the
473	   * unsubscribe. Don't omit the dependency list or put a query built
474	   * during render in it: either one re-subscribes on every render. To
475	   * sort or filter by fast-changing UI state, subscribe once to the
476	   * wider set and derive the view in render.
477	   */
478	  onSnapshot(
479	    next: (snap: DocumentSnapshot) => void,
480	    error?: (e: DbError) => void,
481	  ): Unsubscribe;
482	
483	  /** A subcollection under this document. */
484	  collection(path: string): CollectionReference;
485	};
486	
487	/**
488	 * A filtered, ordered, limited view of one collection. Builders are
489	 * pure — each returns a NEW query; terminal calls do the work.
490	 * Filters and `orderBy` evaluate against top-level fields without
491	 * indexes (the store scans the collection), so keep queried
492	 * collections modest — hundreds to low thousands of documents.
493	 */
494	type Query = {
495	  /** Add a filter (up to 10). Operators: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`,
496	   * `>`, `>=`, `in`, `not-in` (value arrays of at most 30), and
497	   * `array-contains`. */
498	  where(field: string, op: string, value: unknown): Query;
499	
500	  /** Order by one top-level field (at most one `orderBy`);
501	   * `dir` defaults to `"asc"`. Documents missing the field sort
502	   * last. Without `orderBy`, results are ordered by document id
503	   * (ascending) — the same on every delivery path. */
504	  orderBy(field: string, dir?: "asc" | "desc"): Query;
505	
506	  /** At most `n` documents (1-1000). An ordered, limited query is a
507	   * window: documents beyond the window are not delivered until
508	   * they enter it. */
509	  limit(n: number): Query;
510	
511	  /** Read the matched set once, in query order. */
512	  get(): Promise<QuerySnapshot>;
513	
514	  /** Subscribe to the matched set — same delivery contract and same
515	   * subscribe-once rule as {@link DocumentReference.onSnapshot} (in
516	   * React, subscribe inside the effect, never during render, and don't
517	   * list a query built during render as a dependency), with
518	   * `docChanges()` describing each transition. At most 64 active
519	   * subscriptions per view (the 65th rejects `resource_exhausted` on
520	   * the error callback). */
521	  onSnapshot(
522	    next: (snap: QuerySnapshot) => void,
523	    error?: (e: DbError) => void,
524	  ): Unsubscribe;
525	};
526	
527	/** A collection: a {@link Query} over everything in it, plus
528	 * document access and creation. */
529	type CollectionReference = Query & {
530	  path: string;
531	
532	  /** A document in this collection. Omit `id` to mint a fresh
533	   * client-generated id — the retriable-create idiom (the store has
534	   * no idempotency key; a retried create with a fresh ref leaves at
535	   * most one document per id). */
536	  doc(id?: string): DocumentReference;
537	
538	  /** Create a document under a client-generated id and resolve its
539	   * ref. Sugar for `.doc().set(data)`. */
540	  add(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<DocumentReference>;
541	};
542	
543	/**
544	 * The store surface. Refs are pure path holders — building them never
545	 * touches the network; only the calls on them do.
546	 *
547	 * DOCUMENT BODIES are plain-JSON OBJECTS (not arrays or scalars at
548	 * the top level): at most 256 KiB serialized and 32 levels deep.
549	 * CAPACITY: an artifact's database holds at most 25,000 documents in
550	 * total. Don't map an unbounded, growing stream (events, log lines,
551	 * messages) to one document per item — aggregate many items into one
552	 * document or prune old ones — and when a create rejects with
553	 * `quota_exceeded`, tell the viewer what happened and what to do.
554	 * Numbers are JSON numbers (double precision). Writes are
555	 * last-writer-wins — compare document STATE to reason about
556	 * concurrency, never row counts or call counts.
557	 */
558	type DB = {
559	  /** A document reference. The path must have an even number of
560	   * segments (`tasks/t1`); throws `TypeError` for a path that breaks
561	   * the grammar above. */
562	  doc(path: string): DocumentReference;
563	
564	  /** A collection reference. The path must have an odd number of
565	   * segments (`tasks`, `boards/b1/columns`); throws `TypeError` for a
566	   * path that breaks the grammar above. */
567	  collection(path: string): CollectionReference;
568	};
569	
570	interface ClaudeCapabilityMap {
571	  db: DB;
572	}
573

/**
 * The `db` capability — a persistent, realtime document store for this
 * artifact, shared by its viewers.
 *
 * One store per artifact: JSON documents at slash-separated paths
 * (`collection/doc`, nesting deeper as `collection/doc/subcollection/doc`),
 * surviving reloads, republishes, and sessions. The store is created on
 * the first write and erased when the artifact is deleted. Reads and
 * subscriptions see other viewers' writes live. Declare
 * `capabilities: {db: {}}`. Only the owner can write, plus anyone invited
 * by email as an editor (where the share menu offers that level, and only
 * while the artifact is not also shared by a public link), plus,
 * on a plan with other members (such as Team or Enterprise), the members
 * who can open the artifact, unless their sharing level is view-only
 * (`view`). A view-only member can only read shared data, never write it.
 * Anyone else is an outside viewer: they never write, and read shared data
 * only when signed in, through a public link or an email invitation.
 *
 * ACCESS RULES. By default everyone admitted reads shared documents,
 * those at `interact` or above also write them, and each viewer's own
 * `data/users/<id>/` subtree is private.
 * To change who may read or write where, declare rules keyed on the
 * viewer's sharing level — `interact` (the share menu's Contributor: uses
 * the page and changes its shared data), `admin` (the share menu's Editor
 * or Owner: also publishes versions and assets; an Editor from outside
 * the organization, invited by email, holds it only while the artifact
 * is not also shared by link), `owner` (the artifact's own owner; not a
 * person granted Owner), plus `view`, the lowest level, for paths that
 * should stay readable by everyone the server admits (Viewers, Commenters
 * and outside visitors hold `view`; it only ever widens reads, never
 * writes) — as the minimum level for each action at a path and below:
 *   capabilities: { db: { rules: [
 *     { path: "", read: "interact", write: "admin" },
 *     { path: "data/users/{self}", write: "interact" },
 *   ] } }
 * reads "viewers at `interact` or above read shared data, only editors
 * write it, and each of them writes their own subtree". A rule applies
 * to its path and everything below; a deeper rule overrides it there and
 * may be stricter or looser. A level left unset inherits from the nearest
 * rule above (the root defaults to read: "view", write: "interact").
 * A fifth word, `self`, comes with `{self}` below.
 * An artifact created from a type often ships with that type's rules
 * already declared (commonly `write: "admin"` on shared data): read its
 * manifest before assuming the defaults.
 * Inheritance reaches each viewer's own subtree too: with no
 * `data/users/{self}` rule declared it inherits like any other path, so
 * locking the root alone (`{ path: "", write: "admin" }`) also stops
 * everyone below `admin` writing their own subtree. A page where only
 * editors change shared data and each person at Contributor or above
 * still fills in their own part also declares
 * `{ path: "data/users/{self}", write: "interact" }` beside it (each
 * part stays hidden from everyone else, the owner and editors included,
 * unless a rule at `data/users` opens it, see below). Put data that only
 * editors may change under its own path with a raised write level:
 *   { path: "data/editors-only", write: "admin" }
 * It lets everyone who reads shared data read it and only `admin` and
 * above write it, there and below. `data/editors-only` is itself a
 * document path, so keep collections below it, as in
 * `data/editors-only/notes/n1`. Add `read: "admin"` and it reads as
 * non-existent to everyone below `admin`, in `get`, queries and
 * `onSnapshot` alike.
 * Writing implies reading: a rule's write level is never below its read
 * level. A path ending in `/{self}` names each viewer's own subtree under
 * that prefix: nobody else — the artifact's owner included — sees a
 * sibling's subtree unless a rule at the prefix opens it, and `{self}`
 * must be the last segment. `{self}` works under ANY prefix, not only
 * `data/users`: "everyone reads the votes, each viewer writes only
 * their own" is
 *   { path: "votes", read: "view", write: "owner" },
 *   { path: "votes/{self}", write: "interact" }
 * with each viewer writing `votes/<their id>` (or documents below it)
 * and only the owner able to change someone else's; `write: "admin"` on
 * the prefix would also let every Editor, and anyone granted Owner, do
 * so. A rule declared AT the prefix of a `{self}` rule (here `votes`)
 * must set BOTH `read` and `write`, or the declaration is rejected at
 * publish; with no prefix rule, siblings' subtrees stay private as under
 * `data/users`.
 * `self` is a level nobody holds, not even the owner. It goes only on
 * the rule AT the prefix of a declared `{self}` rule (here `votes`),
 * never on the root or on the `{self}` rule itself. On someone else's
 * subtree only the prefix rule applies; on a viewer's own, whichever of
 * the two rules gives them more.
 * Keep `write: "owner"` or `"admin"` on the prefix by default: on most
 * lists (a sign-up sheet, a guestbook, a poll, a Q&A board) somebody must
 * be able to tidy or moderate, and under `write: "self"` nobody can. Use
 * `self` only when the request says that nobody else, the owner included,
 * may change an entry, or that an entry has to be that person's own act
 * (a sign-off, an approval, a consent, a vote nobody may touch), or that
 * nobody else may read it:
 *   { path: "signoffs", read: "view", write: "self" },
 *   { path: "signoffs/{self}", read: "view", write: "interact" }
 * With `write: "self"`, choose `read` by who else should see the
 * documents:
 *   read: "view",  write: "self"   a sign-off sheet: everyone reads,
 *                                  each writes only their own
 *   read: "admin", write: "self"   a suggestion box: each writes only
 *                                  their own, Editors and the owner read
 *                                  them all
 *   read: "self",  write: "self"   a notebook private from the other
 *                                  people on the artifact: nobody else
 *                                  reads or writes it
 * Where nobody else reads, nobody can count: a ballot that someone must
 * count wants the suggestion box's pattern, whose readers see who chose
 * what, or Hidden-until-reveal below. `read: "self"` is valid only with
 * `write: "self"`. Beside a prefix rule that uses `self`, state both
 * levels on the `{self}` rule, as above: they set who writes their own
 * subtree, and who reads it where the prefix's `read` does not already
 * admit them.
 * A viewer who can read only their own `{self}` subtree (a Contributor
 * in the suggestion box, anyone in the notebook) gets just their own
 * documents from a listener or query on the prefix collection.
 * `self` is a rule, not encryption. It stops only other people's direct
 * reads and writes: paths and ids are stored in the clear, page code runs
 * as whoever is viewing, and the owner or any Editor (whoever can publish
 * the artifact or its type, an Editor from outside the organization
 * included) can later publish looser rules or other code, then read or
 * overwrite the documents already stored. Nobody is told. Before loosening
 * a `self` rule, tell whoever asked what it would expose. While
 * `write: "self"` stands, nobody else can correct or remove one viewer's
 * documents, short of deleting the artifact. For data kept from everyone
 * else on the artifact, `data/users/<id>/` is stronger, though not
 * loosening-proof: unless a version declared a rule at `data/users`, or
 * at `data` beside `data/{self}`, nobody else has ever reached it.
 * At most 64 rules; paths follow the
 * document-path grammar below. The owner meets every level but `self`,
 * so only `self` and `{self}` privacy limit the owner. Who holds
 * which level, in the share menu's words (Owner, Editor, Contributor,
 * Commenter, Viewer): Editor and Owner hold `admin`; an Editor from
 * outside the organization, invited by email (where the menu offers
 * that), holds it unless the artifact is also shared by link. A person
 * granted Owner in the share menu holds `admin`, not `owner`, and so do
 * the members who can post in an added channel or project granted it:
 * `owner` is only the artifact's own owner (`isOwner()`). On an artifact
 * a person owns, that is one person; on an artifact Claude made in a
 * channel or project, it is the members of that channel or project who
 * can post in it. The share menu shows the artifact's own owner (that
 * person, or that channel or project) first in its list of who has
 * access, in a row that cannot be changed or removed, whatever level
 * name that row shows.
 * Contributor, on a person or on general access, holds `interact`, as
 * does a member of the organization who arrives by a public link. Viewer
 * and Commenter hold `view`, as does every signed-in visitor from
 * outside the organization, by public link or email invitation, except
 * the outside Editor above while the artifact is not shared by link. On
 * an artifact a person owns, a member whom general access also admits
 * (organization-wide, or by a public link) holds the higher of their own
 * level and the level it gives, so being listed as Viewer or Commenter
 * does not lower them. A person who stays at Commenter under that rule
 * reads and comments and writes no data, their own `data/users/<id>/`
 * subtree included. A signed-out visitor has no data at all. So by
 * default only `interact` and above write shared documents or their own
 * subtree, and a page where each person saves their own data needs them
 * at Contributor or above. A call below the minimum fails the same way
 * as a sibling's `{self}` subtree: a read sees a non-existent document
 * and a write rejects `invalid_argument` —
 * so gate controls up front on what the `user` capability reports
 * (`can("data.write")` = may write shared documents under the root rule;
 * `canEdit()` = admin, for controls a rule reserves for admin;
 * `isOwner()` = owner) rather than branching on the code. When
 * `can("data.write")` resolves null, or `claude.use("user")` itself
 * does, the platform has said nothing about this viewer's write level:
 * keep shared-data inputs, and if a well-formed `set()` then rejects
 * `invalid_argument` render them read-only for the rest of the visit.
 * The rules in force are those of the version readers are served, or the
 * newest version's if that one declares no `db`, from the next call after
 * it goes live; `{db: {}}` restores the defaults. On an artifact made from
 * a type it is the other way round: the newest version's rules apply, or
 * the served version's if the newest declares no `db`.
 * AVAILABILITY is a
 * per-view fact: obtain the namespace with `await claude.use("db")` —
 * it resolves `null` when this view cannot run db (not served, not
 * granted at initialization, or failed to load) — and handle the
 * lifecycle rejection codes on calls and the `onSnapshot` error
 * callback.
 */

/** Rejection shape for every method and the `onSnapshot` error
 * callback. `message` is human-readable but not localized. */
type DbError = {
  code: DbErrorCode;
  message: string;
};

/**
 * Stable error codes. Branch on `code`, never on message text; treat
 * unknown codes as `"unavailable"`.
 *
 * Store codes — the complete set for store operations:
 * - `invalid_argument` — the path, body, or query breaks a rule in
 *   the docs below (bad path grammar, non-object body, a document
 *   over 256 KiB or 32 levels deep, too many filters, an
 *   over-limit page size, ...). Surfaces at call time for verbs
 *   and on the error callback at subscribe time. Fix the call;
 *   retrying cannot succeed.
 * - `resource_exhausted` — a budget: the per-viewer call rate, the
 *   subscription cap (64 per view), too many concurrent writes or
 *   active leases, or a query that scans too many documents. Slow
 *   down, subscribe to less, or narrow the query; tightening a loop
 *   on it cannot succeed.
 * - `quota_exceeded` — a cap is full: documents in the collection,
 *   documents in this artifact's database, the organization's
 *   databases, or the total size of this artifact's database (the
 *   message names which). Not transient: at a count cap creating
 *   documents fails until some are deleted, while writes to existing
 *   documents still succeed; at the size cap creating documents can
 *   fail, and so can a write that makes an existing document larger,
 *   until documents are deleted or made smaller. Surface it to the
 *   viewer; retrying cannot succeed.
 * - `unavailable` — a transient platform condition. Verbs: retry
 *   once after a short randomized delay. Subscriptions handle this
 *   INTERNALLY and in silence (see `onSnapshot`): an error callback
 *   never receives it, EXCEPT when the page's host itself stops
 *   answering: that listener is terminated with `unavailable` and a
 *   fresh `onSnapshot` is the only recovery.
 * - `revoked` — this view's grant was withdrawn while the page was
 *   running (access, sharing, or availability changed). Terminal for
 *   the page load: at most one delivery per listener; calls reject
 *   thereafter. Render the degraded experience; don't editorialize
 *   about why — the surrounding app owns access messaging.
 *
 * There is deliberately NO `permission-denied` and NO not-found code
 * on reads: a document this viewer cannot see behaves exactly like
 * one that does not exist (`exists: false`, omitted from queries).
 *
 * Lifecycle codes (from the runtime itself, not the store):
 * - `not_granted` — this view did not grant db to the frame.
 * - `capability_disabled` — granted but not usable in this view
 *   (the serving runtime predates it or its module failed to load).
 * - `capability_removed` — the called method is not part of the
 *   runtime serving this view; treat like `capability_disabled`.
 * - `transform_error` — the call's arguments could not be prepared;
 *   treat like `invalid_argument`.
 * (`queue_overflow`, from runtimes that queue calls made before they
 * are ready, can also reach an error callback; it is terminal for that
 * listener and falls under the unknown-code rule above.)
 */
type DbErrorCode =
  | "invalid_argument"
  | "resource_exhausted"
  | "quota_exceeded"
  | "unavailable"
  | "revoked"
  | "not_granted"
  | "capability_disabled"
  | "capability_removed"
  | "transform_error";

/**
 * PATH GRAMMAR (shared by every ref). A document path has an EVEN
 * number of slash-separated segments — the last is the document id,
 * the joined rest is its collection (`tasks/t1`, or nested:
 * `boards/b1/columns/c2`). A collection path is the odd-length
 * prefix form (`tasks`, `boards/b1/columns`). Count segments before
 * choosing the builder. `data/users/<id>` (3) is a COLLECTION — the
 * viewer's own — so one document per viewer is
 * `db.doc("data/users/" + uid + "/profile")` (4), and one document per
 * deck is `db.collection("data/users/" + uid).doc(deckId)` (4).
 * `data/users/<id>/decks` (4) is therefore a DOCUMENT path, not a
 * collection: a named per-viewer list is a subcollection under a
 * per-viewer document,
 * `db.doc("data/users/" + uid + "/profile").collection("decks")` (5),
 * each deck `.doc(deckId)` below it (6) — building from a ref like
 * this keeps the parity right for you. Segments use letters, digits,
 * and `_ - . ~ : @ +` only (never `.` or `..` alone); at most
 * 200 bytes per segment, 1000 bytes and 16 segments per path.
 * `doc()`, `collection()` and the builders on refs THROW a
 * `TypeError` synchronously for a path that breaks
 * this grammar (its message names the broken rule; for parity, the
 * segment count) — a programming error to fix where the path is
 * written, not a store condition to handle; building a ref never
 * touches the network. Paths are data you choose — there is no need to
 * pre-create a collection, and deleting a document does NOT delete
 * documents nested under its path.
 *
 * The `data/users/` path prefix is special, platform-side: each
 * viewer's own subtree under it is private per viewer — including
 * from the artifact's owner (the default `data/users/{self}` rule;
 * a declared rule at the `data/users` prefix opens siblings' subtrees
 * at its levels, see ACCESS RULES above). Address the viewer's subtree as
 * `data/users/<id>/...` using the AWAITED value of
 * {@link Claude.user.id} (declare `user` alongside `db` — without
 * the declaration `id()` resolves null; it is async, and an
 * un-awaited promise is not a valid path segment, so the builder
 * throws) — the
 * store recognizes exactly that id as this viewer, no other value
 * works. A null id means no private subtree: disable the per-viewer
 * feature for that visit rather than relocating its data to a
 * shared path; a view-only or comment-only member has an id yet cannot
 * write there either, so treat a rejected write the same way. Another
 * viewer's documents under `data/users/`
 * read as non-existent (`exists: false`, omitted from queries and
 * `onSnapshot`) — the "shared by its viewers" default does NOT
 * apply inside this prefix — and a write (`set`/`update`/`delete`)
 * into another viewer's subtree rejects `invalid_argument`.
 * Hidden-until-reveal (sealed votes, planning poker): each viewer
 * writes their pick under their own `data/users/<id>/` path, where by
 * default nobody else can read it, and copies it to a shared path when
 * THEY reveal — rules are fixed at publish, so nothing a page does at
 * run time opens another viewer's subtree.
 */

/** Snapshot provenance. `fromCache: true` marks a view the store has
 * not confirmed, such as a copy saved on an earlier visit, your own
 * writes before the first read lands, a collection too large to read
 * whole, or delivery during a connectivity gap. A definitive snapshot
 * follows by itself once the store answers in full.
 * `hasPendingWrites` is true while the view includes this page's own
 * unconfirmed write (latency compensation). */
type SnapshotMetadata = {
  fromCache: boolean;
  hasPendingWrites: boolean;
};

/** One document, as reads and snapshots deliver it. Delivered
 *  snapshots and their `data()` are frozen; a document that didn't
 *  change is the same object across deliveries — compare with
 *  `===`, don't mutate or accumulate them (clone a body before
 *  editing it for a write). */
type DocumentSnapshot = {
  /** The last segment of the document's path. */
  id: string;
  /** False covers both a missing document and one this viewer cannot
   * see — deliberately indistinguishable. */
  exists: boolean;
  /** The document body; `undefined` when `exists` is false. */
  data(): Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
  metadata: SnapshotMetadata;
};

/** One ordered-view transition inside a query snapshot. Indexes are
 * positions in the snapshot's `docs` order: `oldIndex` is -1 for
 * `added`, `newIndex` is -1 for `removed`. `removed` covers
 * deletion, leaving the query, and losing visibility, identically; its
 * `doc` is the last snapshot the listener saw (`exists: true`,
 * carrying the final body), so a removal handler still has the data. */
type DocumentChange = {
  type: "added" | "modified" | "removed";
  doc: DocumentSnapshot;
  oldIndex: number;
  newIndex: number;
};

/** A query's matched set, in query order. */
type QuerySnapshot = {
  docs: DocumentSnapshot[];
  size: number;
  empty: boolean;
  /** The changes since the previous snapshot of this listener (the
   * first snapshot is all-`added`). */
  docChanges(): DocumentChange[];
  metadata: SnapshotMetadata;
};

/** Stop receiving snapshots. Idempotent; after it returns, the
 * callbacks never fire again. */
type Unsubscribe = () => void;

type AcquireOptions = {
  /** Who holds the lease — any stable string (a viewer id, a tab
   * id). Renewal requires the same holder. */
  holder: string;
  /** Requested lease length in milliseconds. Absent/0 means 30000;
   * values are clamped to [1000, 600000], never rejected. */
  ttlMs?: number;
  /** Merged into the document body when the lease is granted. */
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
};

type AcquireResult = {
  acquired: boolean;
  /** The document's version after a granted acquire. */
  version?: number;
  /** RFC 3339 expiry of the lease now in force (granted or not). */
  expiresAt?: string;
  /** Your own holder string, echoed on a granted acquire; absent when
   * busy — the platform reveals `expiresAt`, never who holds it. */
  holder?: string;
};

/**
 * A reference to one document. Pure and synchronous to create — a
 * malformed path throws here; nothing reaches the store until a
 * terminal call.
 */
type DocumentReference = {
  /** The last path segment. */
  id: string;
  path: string;

  /** Read once. Absence is NOT an error — branch on `exists`. */
  get(): Promise<DocumentSnapshot>;

  /** Write the WHOLE document, creating it (and the store) if
   * absent — a full replace, Firestore-style. Use `update` to merge
   * into existing fields. Writes are last-writer-wins; there are no
   * transactions.
   *
   * ONE WRITE AT A TIME per document, only when its data changed:
   * await each `set`/`update` before the next to the same document;
   * write on a user action or a real state change, never from render
   * code, a snapshot callback, or a timer that rewrites unchanged or
   * clock-derived values; coalesce a burst of input events into one
   * write per pause. The page open in other tabs or devices writes the
   * same documents; overlapping writes to one document make each write
   * slower. */
  set(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>;

  /** Merge-write that REQUIRES the document to exist — rejects
   * `invalid_argument` otherwise (creating-on-miss would be a bug
   * for its use cases). Nested objects merge recursively; anything
   * else (arrays included) replaces that field wholesale. Same
   * one-write-at-a-time rule as `set`. Do NOT build monotonic
   * counters from read-modify-update — writes are last-writer-wins
   * and a retried write can apply twice. */
  update(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>;

  /** Delete this document. Idempotent; nested documents survive. */
  delete(): Promise<void>;

  /**
   * Cooperative short lease on this document — set-if-not-busy, the
   * single-writer primitive (one editor at a time, a migration that
   * should run once, a turn lock). NOT a security boundary: other
   * viewers can still write directly; leases only coordinate
   * callers that all use `acquire`. Busy resolves
   * `{acquired: false}` — a normal outcome, never an error. Leases
   * expire on their own (no release verb): prefer short `ttlMs`
   * and renew while working. There is no create-if-absent write, so
   * "claim a slot" (a seat, a username, first-come ownership) is:
   * `acquire` the slot document (short `ttlMs`, no `data`), `get()`
   * it, and while you hold the lease `set` your claim only if it does
   * not exist yet or its body names no owner, then let the lease
   * lapse; `{acquired: false}` means someone else is mid-claim — treat
   * the slot as taken or re-read after `expiresAt`. Do not carry the
   * claim in `acquire`'s `data` (it merges on every later grant too).
   * A bare get-then-set races and both callers believe they won.
   */
  acquire(options: AcquireOptions): Promise<AcquireResult>;

  /**
   * Subscribe to this document. `next` fires with the current state
   * once the store answers, then on every change — including other
   * viewers' writes, live. Your own writes appear immediately
   * (`hasPendingWrites: true` until confirmed), and a returning viewer
   * may first get a copy saved on an earlier visit (`fromCache: true`).
   * Delivery rides a realtime stream when available and falls back to
   * periodic refresh (about 30 s foreground) — same callbacks either way.
   * While the store cannot be reached (offline, or a network that
   * holds, drops or blocks its requests) the listener may hear nothing
   * from it, not even an error, and keeps retrying until it answers.
   * So time-limit loading: start a timer of about 10 s when you
   * subscribe. If it fires, say the data can't be reached yet or, over
   * anything already delivered, that it may be out of date. The first
   * snapshot with `fromCache: false` clears the timer and that note; so
   * does `error`, which ends the loading state too. Until `error` fires,
   * keep the listener: never reload the page or subscribe again to
   * recover.
   * `error` receives at most one terminal {@link DbError}
   * (`invalid_argument`, `resource_exhausted`, `revoked`, or the
   * `unavailable` above), after which the subscription
   * is dead. Pass it: without one a terminal error is reported via
   * `reportError` (your `error` event and console see it) and the
   * listener still dies.
   *
   * SUBSCRIBE ONCE per document or query (when the view starts, or
   * when the path or filter really changes), keep the returned
   * `Unsubscribe`, and call it when done. Never subscribe from code
   * that runs on every render (a React component body, a `render()`
   * function, anything the snapshot callback triggers): each call
   * opens another subscription, each snapshot re-renders, and the
   * page loops. In React, subscribe in a `useEffect`, build the ref or
   * query inside it, depend only on stable primitives, and return the
   * unsubscribe. Don't omit the dependency list or put a query built
   * during render in it: either one re-subscribes on every render. To
   * sort or filter by fast-changing UI state, subscribe once to the
   * wider set and derive the view in render.
   */
  onSnapshot(
    next: (snap: DocumentSnapshot) => void,
    error?: (e: DbError) => void,
  ): Unsubscribe;

  /** A subcollection under this document. */
  collection(path: string): CollectionReference;
};

/**
 * A filtered, ordered, limited view of one collection. Builders are
 * pure — each returns a NEW query; terminal calls do the work.
 * Filters and `orderBy` evaluate against top-level fields without
 * indexes (the store scans the collection), so keep queried
 * collections modest — hundreds to low thousands of documents.
 */
type Query = {
  /** Add a filter (up to 10). Operators: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`,
   * `>`, `>=`, `in`, `not-in` (value arrays of at most 30), and
   * `array-contains`. */
  where(field: string, op: string, value: unknown): Query;

  /** Order by one top-level field (at most one `orderBy`);
   * `dir` defaults to `"asc"`. Documents missing the field sort
   * last. Without `orderBy`, results are ordered by document id
   * (ascending) — the same on every delivery path. */
  orderBy(field: string, dir?: "asc" | "desc"): Query;

  /** At most `n` documents (1-1000). An ordered, limited query is a
   * window: documents beyond the window are not delivered until
   * they enter it. */
  limit(n: number): Query;

  /** Read the matched set once, in query order. */
  get(): Promise<QuerySnapshot>;

  /** Subscribe to the matched set — same delivery contract and same
   * subscribe-once rule as {@link DocumentReference.onSnapshot} (in
   * React, subscribe inside the effect, never during render, and don't
   * list a query built during render as a dependency), with
   * `docChanges()` describing each transition. At most 64 active
   * subscriptions per view (the 65th rejects `resource_exhausted` on
   * the error callback). */
  onSnapshot(
    next: (snap: QuerySnapshot) => void,
    error?: (e: DbError) => void,
  ): Unsubscribe;
};

/** A collection: a {@link Query} over everything in it, plus
 * document access and creation. */
type CollectionReference = Query & {
  path: string;

  /** A document in this collection. Omit `id` to mint a fresh
   * client-generated id — the retriable-create idiom (the store has
   * no idempotency key; a retried create with a fresh ref leaves at
   * most one document per id). */
  doc(id?: string): DocumentReference;

  /** Create a document under a client-generated id and resolve its
   * ref. Sugar for `.doc().set(data)`. */
  add(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<DocumentReference>;
};

/**
 * The store surface. Refs are pure path holders — building them never
 * touches the network; only the calls on them do.
 *
 * DOCUMENT BODIES are plain-JSON OBJECTS (not arrays or scalars at
 * the top level): at most 256 KiB serialized and 32 levels deep.
 * CAPACITY: an artifact's database holds at most 25,000 documents in
 * total. Don't map an unbounded, growing stream (events, log lines,
 * messages) to one document per item — aggregate many items into one
 * document or prune old ones — and when a create rejects with
 * `quota_exceeded`, tell the viewer what happened and what to do.
 * Numbers are JSON numbers (double precision). Writes are
 * last-writer-wins — compare document STATE to reason about
 * concurrency, never row counts or call counts.
 */
type DB = {
  /** A document reference. The path must have an even number of
   * segments (`tasks/t1`); throws `TypeError` for a path that breaks
   * the grammar above. */
  doc(path: string): DocumentReference;

  /** A collection reference. The path must have an odd number of
   * segments (`tasks`, `boards/b1/columns`); throws `TypeError` for a
   * path that breaks the grammar above. */
  collection(path: string): CollectionReference;
};

interface ClaudeCapabilityMap {
  db: DB;
}

3	 *
4	 *   const db = await claude.use("db");
5	 *   if (!db) return renderWithoutDb(); // design for absence
6	 *   db.collection("tasks").onSnapshot(render);
7	 *
8	 * Resolves the capability's namespace once this view can run the
9	 * capability's code, or `null` when it cannot: the capability is not
10	 * served on this view, was not granted at initialization, or its module
11	 * failed to load. The null cases are indistinguishable by design —
12	 * design for absence, exactly as `permissions.state()` documents. (Chat
13	 * artifacts use a different, flat `window.claude`; neither `use()` nor
14	 * these namespaces exist there.)
15	 *
16	 * Timing. Inside a viewer the page is framed and `window.claude` exists
17	 * before any of your script runs. Served top-level by the platform, as
18	 * its own page on the artifact's own host, it has the same `use`-only
19	 * `window.claude` before your script too, and every `use()` resolves
20	 * `null` there for now; any other top-level copy of the page (a saved
21	 * file, another host) has no `window.claude` at all. This contract
22	 * promises nothing on it but `use`: treat `window.claude.db`,
23	 * `window.claude.room` and every other capability member as `undefined`
24	 * at every moment. The namespace arrives later, through the promise, once
25	 * the viewer has answered and the module has loaded — never during your
26	 * script's first synchronous run, and not ordered against
27	 * `DOMContentLoaded` either way, so don't assume the DOM is complete
28	 * when it resolves. Render the page without it and light features up

30	 * `null` after 10 s.
