5:The GitHub deletion checks (`CIS.GH.1.2.3` and `CIS.GH.1.2.4`) compare the owners and repository administrators in your organization with the users you have approved. Your organization decides who is trusted and qualified. Maester checks their access and the number of people who have it. 7:Both recommendations are Manual assessments in CIS GitHub Benchmark v1.2.0. The approval configuration supplies the organizational judgment needed for Maester to assess them. The checks only read settings and access; they do not change permissions or attempt deletion. 30: { "Id": "CIS.GH.1.2.3", "Parameters": { "MaximumOrganizationOwners": 3 } }, 31: { "Id": "CIS.GH.1.2.4", "Parameters": { "MaximumOrganizationOwners": 3 } } 63:To run the two checks from a source checkout: 70:Invoke-MtTest -Id 'CIS.GH.1.2.3', 'CIS.GH.1.2.4' -Config ./maester-config.json 80:The maximum defaults to **3**, configurable from **1 through 3** for each test. CIS refers to a "few" owners without specifying a number; this limit is Maester's interpretation. You can approve more users than the limit, but only users who are currently owners count toward it. 84:For issue deletion, GitHub's [documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/organizations/managing-organization-settings/allowing-people-to-delete-issues-in-your-organization) says an organization owner must enable the feature before issues can be deleted. CIS section 1.2.4 still calls for an owner review when `members_can_delete_issues` is `false`. 86:This part of the assessment follows that CIS owner review. It does not determine every user's deletion capabilities or check whether repository policies provide another way to meet the requirement. It needs no repository inventory, custom-role list, repository-policy read or sample issue. 94:Each repository must have **exactly two effective administrators**, both listed in its `ApprovedAdministratorIds`. Effective access includes inherited administrator permissions. Approved users who are not currently administrators do not count toward the total. 128:- An observed count is a minimum, not necessarily the total. Too many distinct owners or administrators, or an observed user outside a configured nonempty approval list, can establish a failure. Fewer than two administrators establishes a failure only when the full list is available and usable. Repository-deletion failures still require the policy review described above. 148:Requests are not retried automatically. Execution failures stop further requests, and concurrent access changes can affect a paginated result. Reaching a collection limit prevents a pass or a failure based only on too few observed administrators; it does not erase an already confirmed excessive count or unapproved user. Repository-deletion failures still depend on the relevant policy review. coderabbitai: 🪄 Fix comments: Fix CodeRabbit comments on this PR

content.text:
CIS asks for less than #2525 enforces. CIS asks you to name trusted people. It never gives a number, and the number limits in the PR are Maester's own.

**What CIS says.** Both items are Manual in CIS GitHub v1.2.0:
- **1.2.3, repository deletion:** "Verify that only a limited number of trusted users can delete repositories." The fix is to allow deletion by "a few trusted and responsible users only."
- **1.2.4, issue deletion:** only "trusted and responsible users" can delete issues.

Neither item says how many owners or admins that should be. My source is the copy of the benchmark text in the Steampipe GitHub compliance mod. The CIS PDF itself needs a login, so I didn't read it. I can't rule out a "two administrators" line in its audit steps.

**What other scanners do:**
- **chain-bench (Aqua)** fails only when the organisation lets members delete repositories (or issues). It doesn't look at who has the access.
- **Steampipe (Turbot)** fails a repository when any of its admins is missing from a trusted-users list you supply. It has no count limit.

**How #2525 compares:**
- **Approved owners and admins list:** this matches what CIS asks, and it's what Steampipe does.
- **At most 3 owners (you can set 1 to 3):** the author made this number up. They say so in the PR, as their reading of CIS's "few".
- **Exactly 2 admins per repository:** this isn't in any public copy of the CIS text. It's the strictest part of the PR and the reason most organisations would fail out of the box.

That backs up the blocking points already in the draft: keep the checks at Investigate until approvals are set up, and question the hard limits. The draft comment still asks the author where "exactly two" comes from.

**Desk:** I've added this comparison as the first finding on the #2525 card and updated it to the new head, 06691925fa53. The author pushed two docs-only commits since the last review, and CI is green: 20 checks passed and 2 were skipped.

Sources:
- [Steampipe: CIS 1.2.3 and 1.2.4 controls](https://github.com/turbot/steampipe-mod-github-compliance/blob/main/cis_supply_chain_v100/section_1.pp) and their [check query](https://github.com/turbot/steampipe-mod-github-compliance/blob/main/query/repo.pp)
- [Steampipe control page for 1.2.3](https://hub.steampipe.io/mods/turbot/github_compliance/controls/control.cis_supply_chain_v100_1_2_3)
- [chain-bench repository-management rules](https://github.com/aquasecurity/chain-bench/tree/main/internal/checks/source-code/repository-management)
- [CISO Assistant CIS GitHub v1.2.0 library](https://github.com/intuitem/ciso-assistant-community/blob/main/backend/library/libraries/cis-benchmark-github.yaml)
- [Xygeni 1.2.3 checkpoint](https://detectors.xygeni.io/xydocs/compliance/checkpoints/cis_sscs/repository_deletion.html)

content.content:
######## 2525
Thanks @thetechgy. The evidence handling here is careful: partial lists can only prove a failure, missing data ends up as Skipped or Investigate and never as a pass, and the deletion guide is thorough.

Before we can merge, a few things need a change or a decision.

- **Blocking: out-of-the-box result for CIS.GH.1.2.3 and 1.2.4.** On main these always return Investigate. With this PR and no config, many orgs will fail:
  - Org owners are effective admins on every repository. With member deletion enabled (GitHub's default), any org with three or more owners fails every repository.
  - An org with more than three owners fails the owner check.

  Without `GitHubDeletionPolicy` the checks can never pass. I'd like them to stay Investigate until approvals are configured, and fail only once the config exists.
- **Blocking: API cost.** With member deletion enabled, the check lists collaborators for every repository even when no config exists and a pass is impossible. On a large org that's thousands of calls on every run. Please stop after the inventory read with Investigate when the policy, or its `Repositories` list, is missing.
- **Blocking: please split the PR.** It changes much more than the GitHub CIS checks:
  - the export and redaction pipeline every suite uses (`Invoke-Maester`, `Get-MtHtmlReport`, `ConvertTo-MtRedactedResult`);
  - a new public parameter, `Add-MtTestResultDetail -RedactedResult`;
  - the shared GitHub transport (rate-limit guard, timeouts, metadata and GraphQL helpers).

  Each of these needs its own review. A suggested split:
  1. the 1.2.2, 1.3.2 and 1.3.8 type fixes, which could merge quickly;
  2. GitHub transport and rate limiting;
  3. redacted results;
  4. the deletion checks and `GitHubDeletionPolicy`.
- **Question: "exactly two administrators" and the 1-3 owner cap.** Is "exactly two" the benchmark's audit wording? If not, please make it configurable or soften it. Capping `MaximumOrganizationOwners` at 3 also means an org whose policy allows more owners can't configure that.
- **For the redacted-results PR:**
  - `TestResultRedacted` is still written to JSON and HTML when redaction is off. Please leave it out of those.
  - For imported results, please fall back to the generic redaction rather than throwing on an invalid value.

---
name: maester-pr-desk
description: Merill's PR review desk for maester365/maester. Use when he asks to "review the new PRs", "update the PR desk", "check which PRs can merge", or "process the PR desk" (act on what he queued). Reviews open PRs, writes a verdict, findings, maintainer fixes and a draft comment for each into the PR Desk artifact, then, once he queues decisions there, posts the reviews, pushes the fixes and merges.
---

# Maester PR Desk

The desk is a published artifact with a small database:
**https://claude.ai/artifact/UohxsGPhGM6VveP4w7ayvo**

The page source is `pr-desk.html`, in this folder. To change the page, edit that file and publish it with the Artifact tool and that `url`; read the artifact first in a new conversation. Read and write its data with the `ArtifactData` tool, using the same `url`.

There are two modes. Merill says which one he wants.

## Mode 1: review ("review the new PRs", "update the desk")

1. **List.** Run `gh pr list --state open` for maester365/maester. Skip drafts; at most, mention them in one line.
   - `ArtifactData list prs` shows what is already on the desk.
   - Review a PR again only if it is new, or its head SHA differs from `prs/<n>.headSha`.
   - If a PR has merged or closed, set `verdict` to `merged` or `closed` and keep its doc as history.
2. **Review.** Fetch each PR's head as `refs/remotes/pr/<n>`: `git fetch origin pull/<n>/head:refs/remotes/pr/<n>`. Never check out over Merill's working branch.
   - Read the existing review threads first, so you don't repeat points that are resolved.
   - Do small PRs inline. Send larger ones to `maester-test-expert` subagents in parallel, read-only.
   - Ask each subagent for: a verdict, the CI cause and fix, behaviour changes against main, findings with file:line, a draft comment, and fixes a maintainer could make.
   - Apply AGENTS.md: the attribute rubric, repository layout, generated files, and benchmark shims. Also check for changes to exported public commands.
   - **Verify the one or two claims that matter** before they go into a comment. For example, read the diff for a "breaking change", or look up Graph permissions with the `msgraph` skill. Don't relay subagent claims unchecked.
   - Check whether CI failures are the PR's fault or come from main. A stale generated file on main is a common cause: `test-builder.json`, `selection.json`, or a broken docs link.
3. **Write** one `prs/<number>` doc per PR, all in a single `ArtifactData batch`, using the schema below.
4. **Report** in chat: a short line per PR, and the desk link. Don't post anything to GitHub in this mode.

## Mode 2: act ("process the PR desk")

1. Run `ArtifactData list decisions` and pick the docs where `status == "queued"`. Ignore `draft` and `hold`.
2. For each one, before acting:
   - If `decision.prSha` or `prs.headSha` differs from the PR's current head on GitHub, stop for that PR. Re-review it, update its doc, set the decision back to `draft` with a note in `prs.outcome`, and tell Merill.
   - Make sure the comment still matches the fixes he ticked. If it still asks the author for a ticked fix (the fix's `ask` phrase), or says "I pushed" for a fix he left unticked, stop and ask him rather than editing his text.
3. **Fixes:** apply each ticked `fixes[].id` on the contributor's branch.
   - Use a worktree under the scratchpad, never the main checkout. The PR must have `maintainerCanModify` set.
   - Prefer merging main to rebasing, so you never force-push over a contributor's history.
   - Regenerate generated files with their build scripts, and run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` before pushing.
   - The commit message ends with the session's Co-Authored-By line.
   - A fix that targets main, like `builder-main`, becomes its own branch and PR off main.
4. **Review:** `event` APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT → `gh pr review <n> --approve|--request-changes|--comment --body-file <file>`. `NONE` → post nothing.
   - The comment is Merill's text, edited on the desk. Post it word for word, then add the block the page shows under "Added below your comment": a blank line, `**Changes I pushed to your branch:**`, then `- <note>` for each ticked fix that isn't `internal`, in `fixes[]` order. Leave the block out if a fix wasn't pushed, and say so in `outcome`.
   - Do the steps in the order the card's "Claude will" box lists them: internal fixes, then the branch fixes, then the review, then the merge.
5. **Merge:** only if `merge` is true and CI is green on the commit you just pushed. Use `gh pr merge <n> --merge`.
   - Never enable auto-merge. If CI is still running, leave the PR and say so.
6. **Record:** update `decisions/<n>` to `status: "done"` with `doneAt`, and `prs/<n>.outcome` with one line on what happened, including links or SHAs.
   - Pin each write to the version you read, with `if_version`.
7. **Report** in chat what was posted, pushed and merged, and anything you skipped and why.

## Data schema

`prs/<number>` is written by Claude:
- **Identity:** `number`, `title`, `author`, `url`, `headSha` (12 chars), `size` (`"+a/-d · n files"`).
- **State:** `merge` (`mergeable|conflicting|behind|blocked`), `ci` (`passing|failing|pending`), `ciNote`.
- **Verdict:** `verdict` (`ready|small-fix|changes|decision|merged|closed`), `order` (rank: ready first, then by complexity).
- **Review:** `reviewedAt` (ISO), `summary`, and `question`, used only when Merill must rule on something.
- **Findings:** `findings[]`, each `{sev: high|medium|low|nit, text, where}`.
- **Fixes:** `fixes[]`, each `{id, text, note, ask, internal, preselect}`. These are things we could do ourselves.
  - `text`: what we'll do, shown beside the checkbox.
  - `note`: the line added to the comment when it's ticked, in the past tense ("Added the missing trailing newline to `x.md`.").
  - `ask`: an exact phrase from the draft comment that asks the author for the same change. The page warns when the fix is ticked and the phrase is still in the comment.
  - `internal: true` for work that isn't on the author's branch (approving fork workflows, merging main before merge). It gets no `note` and isn't mentioned in the comment.
  - Write the draft comment so it reads right with the fixes unticked. The page adds the ticked fixes' notes.
- **Draft:** `event` (`APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT|NONE`) and `comment`, which is markdown for GitHub.
- **History:** `outcome`, a one-line log of the last action.

`decisions/<number>` is written by the page:
- **Review:** `comment`, `event`, `fixes[]` (ticked ids), `merge` (bool).
- **State:** `status` (`draft|queued|hold|done`), `prSha`, `decidedAt`, and `doneAt`, which Claude sets.

Inline text renders `` `code` `` and `**bold**`.

## Writing the comment

- Address the author with their real @login, and thank them once.
- Plain English, short bullets, and bold labels for the blocking items. No emoji, and no headings beyond bold.
- Say clearly what blocks the merge and what is optional.
- When CI fails because of main, tell them it isn't their fault and that we'll fix it.
- Never write "I pushed …" in the comment. The page adds pushed fixes from their `note`, so the comment matches what is ticked.

## Process notes

Merill's rulings go here as they come up.

- Skip contributors' draft PRs.
- Read the existing reviews before reviewing.
- A benchmark test that duplicates another suite's check is a shim.
- No "(Preview)" in test titles.
- Take `headSha` from `git rev-parse --short=12` or `gh`, never typed from memory. A wrong SHA looks like a moved PR.
- A PR that merged after he queued it can't be approved. Post the comment with `gh pr comment` and record that.
- Locally, `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` "skips the family when the module is not installed" fails because the module is installed on his Mac. Ignore it; every other failure blocks a push.
- Write large desk docs from a JSON file (`ArtifactData set` with `file_path`); long inline JSON can fail to parse.
- A contributor who pushes a change and then reverts it may reopen it as a new PR. Compare the two with `git patch-id`.
- Pushing to a contributor's branch dismisses the approvals already on the PR. Re-approve after the push, not before.
- Fork workflows can wait at `action_required` after we push. Approving them is an `internal` fix.

---
name: maester-pr-desk
description: Merill's PR review desk for maester365/maester. Use when he asks to "review the new PRs", "update the PR desk", "check which PRs can merge", or "process the PR desk" (act on what he queued). Reviews open PRs, writes a verdict, findings, maintainer fixes and a draft comment for each into the PR Desk artifact, then, once he queues decisions there, posts the reviews, pushes the fixes and merges.
---

# Maester PR Desk

The desk is a published artifact with a small database:
**https://claude.ai/artifact/UohxsGPhGM6VveP4w7ayvo**

The page source is `pr-desk.html`, in this folder. To change the page, edit that file and publish it with the Artifact tool and that `url`; read the artifact first in a new conversation. Read and write its data with the `ArtifactData` tool, using the same `url`.

There are two modes. Merill says which one he wants.

## Mode 1: review ("review the new PRs", "update the desk")

1. **List.** Run `gh pr list --state open` for maester365/maester. Skip drafts; at most, mention them in one line.
   - `ArtifactData list prs` shows what is already on the desk.
   - Review a PR again only if it is new, or its head SHA differs from `prs/<n>.headSha`.
   - If a PR has merged or closed, set `verdict` to `merged` or `closed` and keep its doc as history.
2. **Review.** Fetch each PR's head as `refs/remotes/pr/<n>`: `git fetch origin pull/<n>/head:refs/remotes/pr/<n>`. Never check out over Merill's working branch.
   - Read the existing review threads first, so you don't repeat points that are resolved.
   - Do small PRs inline. Send larger ones to `maester-test-expert` subagents in parallel, read-only.
   - Ask each subagent for: a verdict, the CI cause and fix, behaviour changes against main, findings with file:line, a draft comment, and fixes a maintainer could make.
   - Apply AGENTS.md: the attribute rubric, repository layout, generated files, and benchmark shims. Also check for changes to exported public commands.
   - **Verify the one or two claims that matter** before they go into a comment. For example, read the diff for a "breaking change", or look up Graph permissions with the `msgraph` skill. Don't relay subagent claims unchecked.
   - Check whether CI failures are the PR's fault or come from main. A stale generated file on main is a common cause: `test-builder.json`, `selection.json`, or a broken docs link.
3. **Write** one `prs/<number>` doc per PR, all in a single `ArtifactData batch`, using the schema below.
4. **Report** in chat: a short line per PR, and the desk link. Don't post anything to GitHub in this mode.

## Mode 2: act ("process the PR desk")

1. Run `ArtifactData list decisions` and pick the docs where `status == "queued"`. Ignore `draft` and `hold`.
2. For each one, before acting:
   - If `decision.prSha` or `prs.headSha` differs from the PR's current head on GitHub, stop for that PR. Re-review it, update its doc, set the decision back to `draft` with a note in `prs.outcome`, and tell Merill.
   - Make sure the comment still matches the fixes he ticked. If it still asks the author for a ticked fix (the fix's `ask` phrase), or says "I pushed" for a fix he left unticked, stop and ask him rather than editing his text.
3. **Fixes:** apply each ticked `fixes[].id` on the contributor's branch.
   - Use a worktree under the scratchpad, never the main checkout. The PR must have `maintainerCanModify` set.
   - Prefer merging main to rebasing, so you never force-push over a contributor's history.
   - Regenerate generated files with their build scripts, and run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` before pushing.
   - The commit message ends with the session's Co-Authored-By line.
   - A fix that targets main, like `builder-main`, becomes its own branch and PR off main.
4. **Review:** `event` APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT → `gh pr review <n> --approve|--request-changes|--comment --body-file <file>`. `NONE` → post nothing.
   - The comment is Merill's text, edited on the desk. Post it word for word, then add the block the page shows under "Added below your comment": a blank line, `**Changes I pushed to your branch:**`, then `- <note>` for each ticked fix that isn't `internal`, in `fixes[]` order. Leave the block out if a fix wasn't pushed, and say so in `outcome`.
   - Do the steps in the order the card's "Claude will" box lists them: internal fixes, then the branch fixes, then the review, then the merge.
   - **Assignee:** when the PR now waits on its author (REQUEST_CHANGES, or a NONE/COMMENT on a PR whose changes are still requested), assign the author: `gh pr edit <n> --add-assignee <author>`. When you approve or merge, remove the author if they are assigned: `--remove-assignee <author>`.
5. **Merge:** only if `merge` is true and CI is green on the commit you just pushed. Use `gh pr merge <n> --merge`.
   - Never enable auto-merge. If CI is still running, leave the PR and say so.
6. **Record:** update `decisions/<n>` to `status: "done"` with `doneAt`, and `prs/<n>.outcome` with one line on what happened, including links or SHAs.
   - Pin each write to the version you read, with `if_version`.
7. **Report** in chat what was posted, pushed and merged, and anything you skipped and why.

## Data schema

`prs/<number>` is written by Claude:
- **Identity:** `number`, `title`, `author`, `url`, `headSha` (12 chars), `size` (`"+a/-d · n files"`).
- **State:** `merge` (`mergeable|conflicting|behind|blocked`), `ci` (`passing|failing|pending`), `ciNote`.
- **Verdict:** `verdict` (`ready|small-fix|changes|decision|merged|closed`), `order` (rank: ready first, then by complexity).
- **Review:** `reviewedAt` (ISO), `summary`, and `question`, used only when Merill must rule on something.
- **Findings:** `findings[]`, each `{sev: high|medium|low|nit, text, where}`.
- **Fixes:** `fixes[]`, each `{id, text, note, ask, internal, preselect}`. These are things we could do ourselves.
  - `text`: what we'll do, shown beside the checkbox.
  - `note`: the line added to the comment when it's ticked, in the past tense ("Added the missing trailing newline to `x.md`.").
  - `ask`: an exact phrase from the draft comment that asks the author for the same change. The page warns when the fix is ticked and the phrase is still in the comment.
  - `internal: true` for work that isn't on the author's branch (approving fork workflows, merging main before merge). It gets no `note` and isn't mentioned in the comment.
  - Write the draft comment so it reads right with the fixes unticked. The page adds the ticked fixes' notes.
- **Draft:** `event` (`APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT|NONE`) and `comment`, which is markdown for GitHub.
- **History:** `outcome`, a one-line log of the last action.

`decisions/<number>` is written by the page:
- **Review:** `comment`, `event`, `fixes[]` (ticked ids), `merge` (bool).
- **State:** `status` (`draft|queued|hold|done`), `prSha`, `decidedAt`, and `doneAt`, which Claude sets.

Inline text renders `` `code` `` and `**bold**`.

## Writing the comment

- Address the author with their real @login, and thank them once.
- Plain English, short bullets, and bold labels for the blocking items. No emoji, and no headings beyond bold.
- Say clearly what blocks the merge and what is optional.
- When CI fails because of main, tell them it isn't their fault and that we'll fix it.
- Never write "I pushed …" in the comment. The page adds pushed fixes from their `note`, so the comment matches what is ticked.

## Process notes

Merill's rulings go here as they come up.

- Skip contributors' draft PRs.
- Read the existing reviews before reviewing.
- A benchmark test that duplicates another suite's check is a shim.
- No "(Preview)" in test titles.
- Take `headSha` from `git rev-parse --short=12` or `gh`, never typed from memory. A wrong SHA looks like a moved PR.
- A PR that merged after he queued it can't be approved. Post the comment with `gh pr comment` and record that.
- Locally, `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` "skips the family when the module is not installed" fails because the module is installed on his Mac. Ignore it; every other failure blocks a push.
- Write large desk docs from a JSON file (`ArtifactData set` with `file_path`); long inline JSON can fail to parse.
- A contributor who pushes a change and then reverts it may reopen it as a new PR. Compare the two with `git patch-id`.
- Pushing to a contributor's branch dismisses the approvals already on the PR. Re-approve after the push, not before.
- Fork workflows can wait at `action_required` after we push. Approving them is an `internal` fix.
- When a PR moves after a decision was `done`, set its decision back to `draft` with the new draft, so it shows under Needs you.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember.ps1
@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+function Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Returns the principals that hold directory roles, with the members of role-assigned groups expanded.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Reads the role assignments with Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment and returns each assigned principal. When a role
+    is assigned to a group, the group's members are returned instead of the group. Role-assignable groups cannot be
+    nested, so one level is read.
+
+    Unlike Get-MtRoleMember, this throws when a group's members cannot be read, so a check cannot pass without
+    evaluating them. A group that no longer exists (404) is skipped.
+
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember -RoleId '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10' -MemberStatus Active
+
+    Returns the principals with an active Global Administrator assignment, including members of role-assigned groups.
+    #>
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
+    param(
+        # The IDs of the role definitions to return members for.
+        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
+        [guid[]]$RoleId,
+
+        # The type of assignments to read. Default is both Eligible and Active.
+        [ValidateSet('Eligible', 'Active', 'EligibleAndActive')]
+        [string]$MemberStatus = 'EligibleAndActive'
+    )
+
+    $roleAssignments = @((Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -RoleId $RoleId -MemberStatus $MemberStatus -ExpandPrincipal -DisableCache).Assignments)
+    foreach ($roleAssignment in $roleAssignments) {
+        $principal = $roleAssignment.principal
+        if ($null -eq $principal) { continue }
+        if ($principal.'@odata.type' -ne '#microsoft.graph.group') {
+            $principal
+            continue
+        }
+
+        try {
+            $groupMembers = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "groups/$($principal.id)/members" -ApiVersion v1.0)
+        } catch {
+            if ($_.Exception.Response.StatusCode -eq 'NotFound') {
+                Write-Verbose "Role-assigned group $($principal.id) was not found and is skipped."
+                continue
+            }
+            throw "Could not read the members of role-assigned group $($principal.id): $($_.Exception.Message)"
+        }
+        foreach ($groupMember in $groupMembers) {
+            if ($null -ne $groupMember) { $groupMember }
+        }
+    }
+}

powershell/public/services/entra/Get-MtRoleMember.ps1
function Get-MtRoleMember {
    <#
    .Synopsis
    Returns all the members of a role.

    .Description
    The role can be either active or eligible, defaults to getting members that are both active and eligible.

    If the assigned member is a group, all members of that group will be returned.

    .Example
    Get-MtRoleMember -Role GlobalAdministrator

    Returns all the Global Administrators and includes both Eligible and Active members.

    .Example
    Get-MtRoleMember -Role GlobalAdministrator -MemberStatus Active

    Returns all the Global Administrators that are currently active and excludes those that are eligible but not yet active.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtRoleMember -Role GlobalAdministrator,PrivilegedRoleAdministrator

    Returns all the Global Administrators and Privileged Role administrators and includes both Eligible and Active members.

    .Example
    Get-MtRoleMember -RoleId "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"

    Returns all the members of the role with the specified RoleId and includes both Eligible and Active members.

    .Example
    Get-MtRoleMember -RoleId "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" -MemberStatus Active

    Returns all the currently active members of the role with the specified RoleId.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Get-MtRoleMember
    #>

    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSReviewUnusedParameter', '', Justification = 'ArgumentCompleter requires the full script block signature, even when only wordToComplete is used.')]
    [CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName = 'RoleName')]
    param(
        # The name of the role to get members for.
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'RoleName', Position = 0, Mandatory = $true)]
        [ArgumentCompleter({
                param($commandName, $parameterName, $wordToComplete)
                Initialize-MtRoleDefinition
                $roleNames = @($script:MtRoles.Keys) + @($script:MtRoleAliases.Keys)
                $roleNames |
                Where-Object { $_.StartsWith($wordToComplete, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) } |
                Sort-Object | ForEach-Object {
                    [System.Management.Automation.CompletionResult]::new($_, $_, 'ParameterValue', $_)
                }
            })]
        [ValidateScript({
                Initialize-MtRoleDefinition
                $roleNames = @($script:MtRoles.Keys) + @($script:MtRoleAliases.Keys)
                if ($_ -in $roleNames) { return $true }
                throw "Unknown role '$_'. Use tab-completion to see valid role names."
            })]
        [string[]]$Role,

        # The ID of the role to get members for.
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'RoleId', Position = 0, Mandatory = $true)]
        [guid[]]$RoleId,

        # The type of members to look for. Default is both Eligible and Active.
        [ValidateSet('Eligible', 'Active', 'EligibleAndActive')]
        [string]$MemberStatus
    )

    # Ensure the role lookup tables are built. Guards against the module-load-time
    # assignment of $script:MtRoles not persisting into the Pester test-execution
    # context (the cause of the MT.1020 NullReferenceException). See Get-MtRoleInfo.
    Initialize-MtRoleDefinition

    Write-Verbose "Getting members for RoleId: $RoleId, Role: $Role, MemberStatus: $MemberStatus"
    if (-not $MemberStatus) { $MemberStatus = 'EligibleAndActive' }

    if ($Role) {
        # Resolve role names to GUIDs via MtRoleDefinition.ToString(), then explicitly cast to [guid[]]
        # to avoid relying on implicit coercion from MtRoleDefinition through the typed parameter variable.
        $RoleId = [guid[]]($Role | ForEach-Object { (Get-MtRoleInfo -RoleName $_).ToString() })
    }

    $roleAssignments = (Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -RoleId $RoleId -MemberStatus $MemberStatus -ExpandPrincipal -DisableCache).Assignments

    foreach ($directoryRoleId in $RoleId) {
        $assignments = @()
        foreach ($roleAssignment in $roleAssignments | Where-Object { $_.roleDefinitionId -eq "$directoryRoleId" }) {
            $principal = $roleAssignment.principal
            if ($null -eq $principal) { continue }

            $members = @($principal)
            if ($principal.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.group') {
                #5/10/2024 - Entra ID Role Enabled Security Groups do not currently support nesting
                # Get-MtGroupMember returns $null when a group cannot be resolved (e.g., GDAP external groups, deleted groups). Skip null results.
                $groupMembers = Get-MtGroupMember -GroupId $principal.id
                if ($null -ne $groupMembers) {
                    $members += $groupMembers
                }
            }

            # Append the type of assignment
            foreach ($member in $members) {
                $member | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name 'AssignmentType' -Value $roleAssignment.AssignmentType -Force
            }
            $assignments += $members
        }

        $assignments | Sort-Object id -Unique
    }
}

content.text:
The main difference is what happens when a role-assigned group's members can't be read. `Get-MtRoleMember` silently drops those people. The new `Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember` stops with an error instead.

| | `Get-MtRoleMember` (existing, public) | `Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember` (new in #2601, internal) |
|---|---|---|
| Where the assignments come from | `Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -ExpandPrincipal` | The same call |
| Group expansion | One level, through `Get-MtGroupMember` | One level, a direct `groups/{id}/members` call |
| **If a group can't be read** (403, throttling, any error) | `Get-MtGroupMember` writes a warning and returns `$null`. The group's members are left out and the check goes on | **Throws**, so the check reports Error |
| Deleted or missing group (404) | Skipped | Skipped |
| How it recognises a 404 | Checks five forms: enum, `'NotFound'`, `404`, the exception's `StatusCode`, and a match on the message | Checks only `Response.StatusCode -eq 'NotFound'` |
| Group object in the output | Returns the group and its members | Returns the members only |
| Extras | `-Role` by name, tags each member with `AssignmentType`, removes duplicates per role | None. Callers remove duplicates themselves |

**Why the author added it:** with the existing function, a CIS check like 1.1.1 (cloud-only admins) or 1.1.4 (admin licences) can pass even though the members of an unreadable admin group were never checked. The new helper makes that case an Error.

**A risk to raise with the author:** the narrower 404 check. `Get-MtGroupMember` checks several forms because a GDAP partner group or a deleted group doesn't always report a 404 the same way. If one of those 404s doesn't match the single form the new helper checks, the helper throws. Then 1.1.1, 1.1.3 and 1.1.4 would report Error on every tenant with a GDAP group assigned to a role, which covers most MSP-managed tenants.

The fix is to reuse `Get-MtGroupMember`'s 404 check: move it into a small shared helper, or copy the same conditions. The author could also skip the separate function and give `Get-MtGroupMember` a way to throw on errors other than 404, but that changes a public command.

The #2525 unit tests are still running in the background.

Should I add the 404 point to the #2601 card as a finding, with a line in the draft comment asking the author to reuse that check?

content.text:
CodeRabbit asked for it. The author didn't come up with it on their own.

**What prompted it.** On 30 October, CodeRabbit flagged a Major issue on 1.1.4: "Do not pass when group membership cannot be read." The case it described:
- An admin role is assigned to a group.
- Reading that group fails with an error that isn't a 404.
- `Get-MtGroupMember` shows a warning and returns nothing, so `Get-MtRoleMember` carries on as if the group had no members.
- The check then passes without ever looking at those admins.

The same gap affects 1.1.1 and 1.1.3.

CodeRabbit offered two fixes: fail when the group can't be expanded, or change the shared commands so they pass the error on. The author picked the first, with a new internal helper. In their words, they did that because `Get-MtGroupMember` and `Get-MtRoleMember` "are public commands used by other checks and by custom tests". They also pointed to our earlier review asking them to leave shared commands alone in this PR. That review was ours, about `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`. The unit tests cover a 403, which throws, and a 404, which is skipped.

**Why reading a group could fail with something other than a 404:**
- **No permission (403).** The run's token can read role assignments but not group membership. Examples are a custom app registration without `GroupMember.Read.All` or `Directory.Read.All`, or a delegated user who can't see the group. This is the realistic case. The PR now lists `Directory.Read.All` as required for 1.1.4.
- **A group in a restricted management administrative unit**, or one with hidden membership, which can return 403 even with directory read.
- **Throttling (429) or a temporary Graph error (5xx)** that the shared request helper doesn't retry.

In each of these cases the right result is Error, not Pass. So the change is sound.

**A correction to my last answer.** I overstated the 404 risk. Both helpers go through the same `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`, which raises the status as an enum. PowerShell's `-eq 'NotFound'` matches that enum. So the single check in the new helper should catch a normal 404, and the five-way check in `Get-MtGroupMember` is extra caution. The one case I can't confirm is a GDAP partner group, which lives in the partner's tenant. I don't know whether it reaches this code as a 404, or as an assignment with no principal, which the helper skips anyway. It's worth asking the author to test that, but it isn't a blocker.

**One more open point.** After that commit, CodeRabbit raised another Major issue that is still open. The group-member call uses the session cache, unlike the role-assignment call just before it, which bypasses the cache. So if someone is added to an admin group during a session, a later run in that session might miss them. The fix is a one-line `-DisableCache`. That's a better thing to raise on #2601 than the 404 point.

The #2525 unit tests are still running in the background.

Should I add the caching point and the GDAP question to the #2601 card and its draft comment?

fix(entra): keep MT.1210 role assignments on the Graph cache

Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment disabled the Graph cache for every caller and
dropped $select, so MT.1210 no longer reused the roleAssignments response that
MT.1209 caches. The helper now uses the cache unless -DisableCache is passed and
forwards -Select. Get-MtRoleMember passes -DisableCache as it did before, and
MT.1210 selects the same properties as MT.1209.

You're right on both counts. CodeRabbit's `-DisableCache` suggestion goes against how Maester is meant to work. And `Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember` is almost entirely a copy of `Get-MtRoleMember`.

## Places that skip the cache during a run (on main)

**Checks that pass `-DisableCache` themselves (13):**

| Check | Request |
|---|---|
| CIS.M365.5.1.2.2, 5.1.2.3, 5.1.4.6, 5.1.5.1, 5.1.6.2 | `policies/authorizationPolicy`. The same request five times, and every one goes to Graph again. |
| CIS.M365.1.3.4 | `admin/appsAndServices/settings` |
| CIS.M365.1.3.5 | `admin/forms/settings` |
| CIS.M365.1.3.7 | `servicePrincipals` filtered to one appId |
| CIS.M365.4.1 | `deviceManagement/settings` |
| CIS.M365.5.1.5.2 | `policies/adminConsentRequestPolicy` |
| CIS.M365.5.2.3.5 | `policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy` |
| MT.1024 | `directory/recommendations?$expand=impactedResources` |
| MT.1059 | `security/identities/healthIssues` |

**Shared helpers:**
- **`Get-MtRoleMember.ps1:86`** calls `Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment … -DisableCache`. That affects eight checks: CIS 1.1.1 and 1.1.3, CISA AAD 7.1 to 7.3, MT.1020, MT.1189 and MT.1192. My commit `bd7eaf70d` on 17 October kept that switch only because it was already there; it had no reason of its own.
- **The new `Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember`** in #2601 copies the same `-DisableCache`.

**These can stay:**
- `Invoke-MtGraphRequest.ps1:175` skips the cache only for `nextLink` pages, because skip tokens repeat. The whole result is still cached afterwards.
- The `-DisableCache` and `-ClearCache` switches on `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`, `Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy`, `Get-MtPrivateAccessApplication`, `Get-MdeConfiguration`, `Invoke-MtGitHubRequest` and `Get-MtSpo` are options a caller can choose. No check passes them.

**One thing to watch when removing the switch from `Get-MtRoleMember`.** It adds an `AssignmentType` property with `Add-Member -Force` to each principal object. Once those objects come from the cache, every caller would be changing the same shared objects. That's mostly harmless, because each call sets the value again, but it's worth a unit test.

## Get-MtRoleMember and Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember compared

Most of the new function's 53 lines are the same as the existing function:
- the same `Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -ExpandPrincipal -DisableCache` call;
- the same loop;
- the same skip for an assignment with no principal;
- the same one-level group expansion.

What's different:
1. **Reading a group.** The new function calls `groups/{id}/members` directly. The existing one goes through `Get-MtGroupMember`, which first reads `groups/{id}`, then its members.
2. **The only real change: it throws on errors other than 404.** `Get-MtGroupMember` shows a warning and returns `$null` on any error, so the group's admins are silently left out.
3. **Things it drops:** there's no `-Role` by name and no `AssignmentType`, results aren't grouped or de-duplicated per role, and the group object itself isn't returned.

**Why the author did it this way.** CodeRabbit said a 403 on a group lets 1.1.4 pass without checking the admins in that group. The author didn't want to change `Get-MtGroupMember` or `Get-MtRoleMember` because they're public commands. They also took our earlier "keep shared behaviour unchanged" comment as applying here, though it was only about `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`. So they copied the function and changed one line's worth of behaviour.

**The real bug is in `Get-MtGroupMember`.** Turning a 403 into "no members" is a false pass for all eight checks above, not just the three CIS ones in #2601. The clean fix is to make `Get-MtGroupMember` throw on errors other than 404, keeping its fuller 404 and GDAP handling. Then `Get-MtRoleMember` throws too, and #2601 can drop the new function and keep calling `Get-MtRoleMember`. That changes how a public command behaves, but the only change is that an unreadable group now reports Error instead of quietly passing.

function Test-MtGraphNotFoundError {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Internal: Returns whether a Microsoft Graph ErrorRecord is a 404 Not Found.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Checks the response status code in its enum, string and integer forms, then the exception's own StatusCode
    property, then the message, because the form depends on the Graph SDK and PowerShell version.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The ErrorRecord caught from a Graph request.
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord]$ErrorRecord
    )

    $responseStatusCode = $ErrorRecord.Exception.Response.StatusCode
    $exceptionStatusCode = $ErrorRecord.Exception.StatusCode
    return ($responseStatusCode -eq [System.Net.HttpStatusCode]::NotFound) -or
        ($responseStatusCode -eq 'NotFound') -or
        ($responseStatusCode -eq 404) -or
        ($exceptionStatusCode -eq [System.Net.HttpStatusCode]::NotFound) -or
        ($ErrorRecord.Exception.Message -match 'NotFound|404')
}

| CIS.M365.1.3.5 | `admin/forms/settings` |
| CIS.M365.1.3.7 | `servicePrincipals` filtered by appId |
| CIS.M365.4.1 | `deviceManagement/settings` |
| CIS.M365.5.1.5.2 | `policies/adminConsentRequestPolicy` |
| CIS.M365.5.2.3.5 | `policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy` |
| MT.1024 | `directory/recommendations?$expand=impactedResources` |
| MT.1059 | `security/identities/healthIssues` |

`Get-MtRoleMember` reads role assignments with `-DisableCache`, which affects every check that uses it (CIS 1.1.1 and 1.1.3, CISA MS.AAD.7.1 to 7.3, MT.1020, MT.1189, MT.1192).

A 403 (missing `GroupMember.Read.All` or `Directory.Read.All`, a restricted administrative unit) or a 429 makes a group look empty, so a check that counts role holders or admins can pass without reading them. `Get-MtRoleMember` inherits this. - Make `Get-MtGroupMember` throw on errors other than 404, for the group, its members and nested groups.

Fixes #2624.

**Checks read through the session cache**

Maester reports on one snapshot of the tenant, so checks must not bypass the Graph cache. This removes `-DisableCache` from 13 checks (CIS.M365.1.3.4, 1.3.5, 1.3.7, 4.1, 5.1.2.2, 5.1.2.3, 5.1.4.6, 5.1.5.1, 5.1.5.2, 5.1.6.2, 5.2.3.5, MT.1024, MT.1059) and from `Get-MtRoleMember`. The five checks that read `policies/authorizationPolicy` now share one request.

**New unit test: `powershell/tests/general/GraphCacheUsage.Tests.ps1`**

It parses every `.ps1` under `tests/`, `packs/`, `powershell/public` and `powershell/internal` and fails when:

- a file outside the allow list mentions `DisableCache` anywhere outside comments: a switch, a parameter, a splat key or a variable;
- a file on the allow list passes a bare `-DisableCache` switch instead of forwarding its caller's choice (`-DisableCache:$DisableCache`).

The allow list is the transport helpers that offer the switch to callers: `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`, `Invoke-MtGraphRequestCache`, `Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment`, `Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy`, `Get-MtPrivateAccessApplication`, `Get-MdeConfiguration` and `Invoke-MtGitHubRequest`. Only `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` may pass the bare switch, for `nextLink` pages. Against main the test fails on all 14 call sites removed here.

**Group lookups stop hiding read errors**

`Get-MtGroupMember` returned `$null` with a warning on any error, so a 403 or 429 made a role-assigned group look empty, and a check that counts role holders could pass without reading them. It now:

- skips a group that is not found (404), such as a deleted group or an external GDAP group, as before;
- throws on any other error reading the group, its members or a nested group.

`Get-MtRoleMember` inherits this. The 404 test that was inline in `Get-MtGroupMember` is now `Test-MtGraphNotFoundError` (internal), used for both reads.

**Behaviour change**

`Get-MtGroupMember` and `Get-MtRoleMember` are public. A custom test that calls them now gets an error, instead of an empty result, when a group can't be read. Checks that use them (CIS 1.1.1 and 1.1.3, CISA MS.AAD.7.1 to 7.3, MT.1020, MT.1189, MT.1192 and `Get-MtPrivilegedRoleUser`) report Error in that case instead of a possible false pass.

**Validation**

`./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`: 5,658 tests, 1 failure, the ZeroTrustAssessment "skips the family when the module is not installed" test, which fails locally because the module is installed.

- skips a group that is not found (404), such as a deleted group or an external GDAP group, as before;
- throws on any other error reading the group, its members or a nested group.

`Get-MtRoleMember` inherits this. The 404 test that was inline in `Get-MtGroupMember` is now `Test-MtGraphNotFoundError` (internal), used for both reads.

**Behaviour change**

`Get-MtGroupMember` and `Get-MtRoleMember` are public. A custom test that calls them now gets an error, instead of an empty result, when a group can't be read. Checks that use them (CIS 1.1.1 and 1.1.3, CISA MS.AAD.7.1 to 7.3, MT.1020, MT.1189, MT.1192 and `Get-MtPrivilegedRoleUser`) report Error in that case instead of a possible false pass.

`./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`: 5,658 tests, 1 failure, the ZeroTrustAssessment "skips the family when the module is not installed" test, which fails locally because the module is installed.

content.text:
I've opened the issue and the PR, and pushed the clean-up to #2601. CI is still running on both PRs.

**Issue [#2624](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/2624)** lists the 13 checks and `Get-MtRoleMember` that turn the cache off, and `Get-MtGroupMember` treating any error as an empty group.

**PR [#2625](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2625)** fixes #2624:
- **Cache:** `-DisableCache` is gone from the 13 checks and from `Get-MtRoleMember`. The five CIS checks that read `policies/authorizationPolicy` now share one request.
- **New unit test, `GraphCacheUsage.Tests.ps1`.** It reads every `.ps1` under `tests/`, `packs/`, `powershell/public` and `powershell/internal`. It fails on two things:
  - Any mention of `DisableCache` outside the allow list, other than in comments.
  - A bare `-DisableCache` passed from a file on the allow list. Only `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` may do that, for its `nextLink` pages.

  The allow list is the seven transport helpers that only offer the switch to their callers. Run against main, the test fails on all 14 places this PR fixes.
- **Group lookups:**
  - `Get-MtGroupMember` still skips a group that isn't found (404). It now throws on any other error reading the group, its members or a nested group, and `Get-MtRoleMember` inherits that.
  - The 404 check moved into a shared internal `Test-MtGraphNotFoundError`, so both lookups use the same logic.
  - New unit tests cover 404, 403 and 429, nested groups, and the cache.
- **Behaviour change:** `Get-MtGroupMember` and `Get-MtRoleMember` are public commands. A custom test calling them now gets an error, not an empty result, when a group can't be read. The PR description says so.
- **Unit tests:** 5,658 run. The only failure is the ZeroTrustAssessment test, which fails on your Mac because the module is installed there.

**#2601: I pushed `898dc4c` to the author's branch.**
- **Removed:** `Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember` and its tests.
- **Changed:** CIS 1.1.1, 1.1.3 and 1.1.4 use `Get-MtRoleMember` again. Their unit tests now mock it, and each has a test that the check errors when the role members can't be read.
- **Kept:** the author's other changes, such as the unique-user count and the empty-role guard.
- **Unit tests:** the same single local failure.
- **Merge #2625 first.** Until #2625 lands, the new .md lines in #2601 that say the check "reports an error" when a group can't be read aren't true yet.

**#2601 on the desk:** the card is a draft with an updated comment. The comment explains the push and points to #2625. It also asks the author not to add CodeRabbit's `-DisableCache`, and approves on the condition that #2625 merges first. Queue it when you're happy with the wording.

6.2.1 Ensure all forms of mail forwarding are blocked and/or
disabled (Automated)
Profile Applicability:
• E3 Level 1
• E5 Level 1
Description:
Exchange Online offers several methods of managing the flow of email messages.
These are Remote domain, Transport Rules, and Anti-spam outbound policies. These
methods work together to provide comprehensive coverage for potential automatic
forwarding channels:
• Outlook forwarding using inbox rules.
• Outlook forwarding configured using OOF rule.
• OWA forwarding setting (ForwardingSmtpAddress).
• Forwarding set by the admin using EAC (ForwardingAddress).
• Forwarding using Power Automate / Flow.
Ensure a Transport rule and Anti-spam outbound policy are used to block mail
forwarding.
NOTE: Any exclusions should be implemented based on organizational policy.
Rationale:
Attackers often create these rules to exfiltrate data from your tenancy, this could be
accomplished via access to an end-user account or otherwise. An insider could also use
one of these methods as a secondary channel to exfiltrate sensitive data.
Impact:
Care should be taken before implementation to ensure there is no business need for
case-by-case auto-forwarding. Disabling auto-forwarding to remote domains will affect
all users in an organization. Any exclusions should be implemented based on
organizational policy.
=====PAGE 432=====
Audit:
Note: Audit is a two step procedure as follows:
STEP 1: Transport rules
To audit using the UI:
1. Select Exchange to open the Exchange admin center.
2. Select Mail Flow then Rules.
3. Review the rules and verify that none of them are forwards or redirects e-mail to
external domains.
To audit using PowerShell:
1. Connect to Exchange online using Connect-ExchangeOnline.
2. Run the following PowerShell command to review the Transport Rules that are
redirecting email:
Get-TransportRule | Where-Object {$_.RedirectMessageTo -ne $null} | ft
Name,RedirectMessageTo
3. Verify that none of the addresses listed belong to external domains outside of the
organization. If nothing returns then there are no transport rules set to redirect
messages.
STEP 2: Anti-spam outbound policy
To audit using the UI:
1. Navigate to Microsoft 365 Defender https://security.microsoft.com/
2. Expand E-mail & collaboration then select Policies & rules.
3. Select Threat policies > Anti-spam.
4. Inspect Anti-spam outbound policy (default) and ensure Automatic
forwarding is set to Off - Forwarding is disabled
5. Inspect any additional custom outbound policies and ensure Automatic
forwarding is set to Off - Forwarding is disabled, in accordance with the
organization's exclusion policies.
To audit using PowerShell:
1. Connect to Exchange online using Connect-ExchangeOnline.
2. Run the following PowerShell cmdlet:
Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy | ft Name, AutoForwardingMode
3. In each outbound policy verify AutoForwardingMode is Off.
=====PAGE 433=====
Note: According to Microsoft if a recipient is defined in multiple policies of the same
type (anti-spam, anti-phishing, etc.), only the policy with the highest priority is applied to
the recipient. Any remaining policies of that type are not evaluated for the recipient
(including the default policy). However, it is our recommendation to audit the default
policy as well in the case a higher priority custom policy is removed. This will keep the
organization's security posture strong.
Remediation:
Note: Remediation is a two step procedure as follows:
STEP 1: Transport rules
To remediate using the UI:
1. Select Exchange to open the Exchange admin center.
2. Select Mail Flow then Rules.
3. For each rule that redirects email to external domains, select the rule and click
the 'Delete' icon.
To remediate using PowerShell:
1. Connect to Exchange Online using Connect-ExchangeOnline.
2. Run the following PowerShell command:
Remove-TransportRule {RuleName}
STEP 2: Anti-spam outbound policy
To remediate using the UI:
1. Navigate to Microsoft 365 Defender https://security.microsoft.com/
2. Expand E-mail & collaboration then select Policies & rules.
3. Select Threat policies > Anti-spam.
4. Select Anti-spam outbound policy (default)
5. Click Edit protection settings
6. Set Automatic forwarding rules dropdown to Off - Forwarding is
disabled and click Save
7. Repeat steps 4-6 for any additional higher priority, custom policies.
=====PAGE 434=====
To remediate using PowerShell:
1. Connect to Exchange Online using Connect-ExchangeOnline.
2. Run the following PowerShell command:
Set-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy -Identity {policyName} -AutoForwardingMode
Off
3. To remove AutoForwarding from all outbound policies you can also run:
Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy | Set-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy -
AutoForwardingMode Off
References:
1. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/mail-flow-
rules/mail-flow-rules

know-about-automatic-email-forwarding-in/ba-

6.2.2 Ensure mail transport rules do not whitelist specific domains
(Automated)
Profile Applicability:
• E3 Level 1
• E5 Level 1
Description:
Mail flow rules (transport rules) in Exchange Online can be configured to set the spam
confidence level (SCL) of a message to -1, which bypasses spam and phishing filtering.
When a rule applies this action to messages based on the sender's domain, all mail
from that domain is treated as trusted and skips anti-malware and anti-phishing
evaluation regardless of message content.
Rationale:
Whitelisting domains in transport rules bypasses regular malware and phishing
scanning, which can enable an attacker to launch attacks against your users from a
safe haven domain.
Note: If an organization identifies a business need for an exception, the domain should
only be whitelisted if inbound emails from that domain originate from a specific IP
address. These exceptions should be documented and regularly reviewed.
Impact:
Removing SCL bypass rules will subject previously whitelisted domains to standard
spam and phishing filtering. Mail from those domains that does not pass filtering may be
quarantined or rejected, which could disrupt established business communications.
Prior to removal, identify any rules in scope and coordinate with affected business
owners. If a legitimate need exists, consider replacing domain-based whitelisting with
approved sender lists at the connection level.
=====PAGE 436=====
Audit:
To audit using the UI:
1. Navigate to Exchange admin center https://admin.exchange.microsoft.com
2. Click to expand Mail Flow and then select Rules.
3. Review each rule and ensure that a single rule does not contain both of these
properties together:
o Under Apply this rule if: Sender's address domain portion belongs
to any of these domains: '<domain>'
o Under Do the following: Set the spam confidence level (SCL) to
'
-1'
Note: Setting the spam confidence level to -1 indicates the message is from a trusted
sender, so the message bypasses spam filtering. The recommendation fails if any
external domain has a SCL of -1.
To audit using PowerShell:
1. Connect to Exchange online using Connect-ExchangeOnline.
2. Run the following PowerShell command:
Get-TransportRule | Where-Object { $_.setscl -eq -1 -and $_.SenderDomainIs -
ne $null } | ft Name,SenderDomainIs,SetSCL
3. Transport rules that fail the audit will be shown. If no output is shown, the
recommendation passes. To pass, all rules with SetSCL set to -1 must not
include any domains in the SenderDomainIs property.
Remediation:
To remediate using the UI:
1. Navigate to Exchange admin center https://admin.exchange.microsoft.com
2. Click to expand Mail Flow and then select Rules.
3. For each rule that sets the spam confidence level to -1 for a specific domain,
select the rule and click Delete.
To remediate using PowerShell:
1. Connect to Exchange online using Connect-ExchangeOnline.
2. To remove a specific non-compliant rule:
Remove-TransportRule -Identity "RuleName"

content.text:
I've read both sections in your CIS M365 v7.0.0 PDF. Its audit steps answer the question, and they say something different from what we told the authors.

**6.2.1 (block mail forwarding), step 2: outbound spam policies**
- In the portal: check the Default policy, then "any additional custom outbound policies… in accordance with the organization's exclusion policies".
- In PowerShell: run `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy | ft Name, AutoForwardingMode`, then "In each outbound policy verify AutoForwardingMode is Off."
- CIS adds a note: only the highest-priority policy applies to a user, but you should audit the Default policy anyway in case a custom policy is removed later.

So 6.2.1 means **every outbound policy**, whether or not any user receives it.

**2.1.15 (outbound message limits)**
- In the portal and in PowerShell, it checks only the Default policy: `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy -Identity Default`.

So 2.1.15 means **the Default policy only**.

**What we decided in #2410, now on main**
- 6.2.1 checks the Default policy, plus custom policies that have an enabled rule, meaning the policies users actually receive. CodeRabbit argued for this and we agreed. It's narrower than CIS asks, because an unused custom policy that allows forwarding passes.

**How that affects the open PRs**
- **#2620** puts 6.2.1 back to checking every policy. That matches CIS exactly, and the author's new remediation is copied from the CIS remediation.
- **#2619**: our request-changes review asked the author to keep custom policies in 2.1.15, "or point to the v7 audit text that limits it to Default". That text exists, so the author was right to check Default only.

**A rule that keeps us consistent**

A CIS check should do what the benchmark's PowerShell audit step does. Where that step is broader than what users actually receive, as in 6.2.1, we stay broad. CIS tells organisations to handle exceptions through their own policy, and Maester shouldn't quietly decide that for them. Where it's narrower, as in 2.1.15, we stay narrow. Our own judgement about the policies users actually receive belongs in MT checks, not CIS ones.

The PowerShell step is the right reference because it's the automatable part of an "Automated" recommendation. It's also usually the most precise wording CIS gives.

Under that rule:
- **#2620:** keep the stricter 6.2.1, untick `restore-active-filter`, and approve once the tabs are fixed.
- **#2619:** drop our 2.1.15 point. Tell the author the v7 audit reads only the Default policy, so their change is right.

The 2.1.6 point in the same #2619 comment needs checking against its own audit text the same way.

content.content:
### A requirement another suite already checks (shims)

Benchmarks overlap: CIS, CISA, ASD and Maester tests often read the same setting. Before writing a check for a
benchmark requirement, and when reviewing one:

1. **Find the tests in every suite that read the setting.** `Get-MtTest -Product <key> -Feature <key> |
   Format-Table Id, Title`, and search `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or setting name.
2. **Read the benchmark's own sources**, not only the requirement's one-line text: its audit or assessment
   guidance and any reference configuration it publishes (CIS audit and remediation sections; the SCuBA baseline
   and ScubaGear; for ASD the ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure
   Cloud). Note every concrete value: a number of days, a threshold, a role list, an authentication strength, a
   rule that must be Block. Use the web tools; cite the page.
3. **Decide:**
   - Same check: write a **shim**, a test with its own `Id`, `Title`, `Control`, `Author` and `.md` whose body is
     `return <the other test's function>` (`return Test-MtCisMfaForEveryUser`).
   - Same check, different value that the other test takes as a parameter: a shim with its own parameter whose
     default is the benchmark's value, passed on (`return Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold $MaximumLockoutThreshold`).
   - Something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers: a check of its own. Read data through
     `internal/services/<service>/` helpers, and move a helper there (with a neutral name) when another suite
     already has the code; never copy another check's logic or name a generic helper after a suite.

A shim declares the same `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`,
`UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `TenantType`, `Cloud`,
`Platform`, `Lifecycle`, `LongRunning` and `Exclusive` as the test it calls; calls a test that is not a shim;
passes only parameters that test declares; leaves its own requirement off that test's `Control`; and says in its
`.md` what the benchmark asks and which test it runs, by ID. `powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1`
enforces all of this. The full guidance, with an example, is
[Tests that another suite already has](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).

When reviewing, fail a benchmark check that re-implements a check another suite already has when the benchmark's
sources give no reason for the difference, and say which test it duplicates and which source you read.

### Where the keys come from
## Validation Checklist

### Test logic
- [ ] Returns exactly one `$true`/`$false`; no stray pipeline output.
- [ ] No other suite already checks the same setting; or the benchmark's own sources were read and the check is
      a shim of that test, or differs from it for a reason those sources give.
- [ ] No `Test-MtConnection` guard, no `Get-MtLicenseInformation` check; `Service` and `License` declared instead.
- [ ] No blanket `try { } catch { Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error ... }`.
- [ ] `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` (not `$null`) when the check does not apply.
- [ ] Data retrieval uses `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or Maester helpers.
- [ ] No hard-coded GUIDs, tenant IDs or names; tunables are described parameters.
- [ ] No writes to `$script:`, `$global:`, `$env:` or `$__MtSession`.
- [ ] `Platform = 'Windows'` if it uses Windows-only commands.

### Attribute and files
- [ ] `Test.<Id>.ps1` and `Test.<Id>.md` in the right suite folder; ID unique and not reused.

## Tests that another suite already has

Benchmarks overlap. CIS, CISA SCuBA and ASD all ask for multifactor authentication for every user, and Maester
has its own test for it as well. Before you write a test for a benchmark requirement, look for a test that
already reads the same setting, then decide from the benchmark's own sources whether it asks for anything that
test does not check.

1. **Find the tests that read the setting.** `Get-MtTest -Product entra -Feature conditional-access | Format-Table
   Id, Title` lists the candidates; searching `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or the setting name finds the rest.
   Look in every suite, not only the one you are writing for.
2. **Read what the benchmark asks, in its own sources.** The one-line text of a requirement is usually generic.
   The detail that decides between two implementations is in the benchmark's audit or assessment guidance and in
   any reference configuration it publishes: the audit and remediation sections of a CIS benchmark, the SCuBA
   baseline and ScubaGear for CISA, and for ASD the ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD
   Blueprint for Secure Cloud. Note every concrete value they name: a number of days, a threshold, a list of

## What a benchmark test evaluates

A CIS test does what the benchmark's **PowerShell audit procedure** does: it reads the same objects and passes on
the same condition. The PowerShell steps are the part of an Automated recommendation that can be automated, and
usually its most precise wording. When the UI steps and the PowerShell steps differ, follow the PowerShell steps.

- **Scope.** When the audit reads every object, the test reads every object, including ones that apply to no
  user. CIS 6.2.1 runs `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy` and checks `AutoForwardingMode` on each policy, so
  the test checks custom policies that have no rule. When the audit reads one object, the test reads only that
  one: CIS 2.1.15 runs `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy -Identity Default`, so the test does not evaluate
  custom policies. Don't narrow a test to the policies users receive, or widen it beyond what the audit reads.
  CIS leaves exceptions to the organization, so a test does not decide them for it.
- **Values.** Use the thresholds the audit names or its script sets, such as the 90% of the extension list in
  CIS 2.1.11. When organizations may need a different value, make it a parameter with the benchmark's value as
  its default.
- **Missing data.** When the object the audit reads is not returned, the test fails or reports an error. It never
  passes because there was nothing to check.

A view of the policies users actually receive belongs in a Maester (MT) test, not in a benchmark test. The same
rule applies to CISA tests, with the SCuBA baseline and ScubaGear's policy in place of the CIS audit procedure.

---
name: maester-pr-desk
description: Merill's PR review desk for maester365/maester. Use when he asks to "review the new PRs", "update the PR desk", "check which PRs can merge", or "process the PR desk" (act on what he queued). Reviews open PRs, writes a verdict, findings, maintainer fixes and a draft comment for each into the PR Desk artifact, then, once he queues decisions there, posts the reviews, pushes the fixes and merges.
---

# Maester PR Desk

The desk is a published artifact with a small database:
**https://claude.ai/artifact/UohxsGPhGM6VveP4w7ayvo**

The page source is `pr-desk.html`, in this folder. To change the page, edit that file and publish it with the Artifact tool and that `url`; read the artifact first in a new conversation. Read and write its data with the `ArtifactData` tool, using the same `url`.

There are two modes. Merill says which one he wants.

## Mode 1: review ("review the new PRs", "update the desk")

1. **List.** Run `gh pr list --state open` for maester365/maester. Skip drafts; at most, mention them in one line.
   - `ArtifactData list prs` shows what is already on the desk.
   - Review a PR again only if it is new, or its head SHA differs from `prs/<n>.headSha`.
   - If a PR has merged or closed, set `verdict` to `merged` or `closed` and keep its doc as history.
2. **Review.** Fetch each PR's head as `refs/remotes/pr/<n>`: `git fetch origin pull/<n>/head:refs/remotes/pr/<n>`. Never check out over Merill's working branch.
   - Read the existing review threads first, so you don't repeat points that are resolved.
   - Do small PRs inline. Send larger ones to `maester-test-expert` subagents in parallel, read-only.
   - Ask each subagent for: a verdict, the CI cause and fix, behaviour changes against main, findings with file:line, a draft comment, and fixes a maintainer could make.
   - Apply AGENTS.md: the attribute rubric, repository layout, generated files, and benchmark shims. Also check for changes to exported public commands.
   - **Verify the one or two claims that matter** before they go into a comment. For example, read the diff for a "breaking change", or look up Graph permissions with the `msgraph` skill. Don't relay subagent claims unchecked.
   - Check whether CI failures are the PR's fault or come from main. A stale generated file on main is a common cause: `test-builder.json`, `selection.json`, or a broken docs link.
3. **Write** one `prs/<number>` doc per PR, all in a single `ArtifactData batch`, using the schema below.
4. **Report** in chat: a short line per PR, and the desk link. Don't post anything to GitHub in this mode.

## Mode 2: act ("process the PR desk")

1. Run `ArtifactData list decisions` and pick the docs where `status == "queued"`. Ignore `draft` and `hold`.
2. For each one, before acting:
   - If `decision.prSha` or `prs.headSha` differs from the PR's current head on GitHub, stop for that PR. Re-review it, update its doc, set the decision back to `draft` with a note in `prs.outcome`, and tell Merill.
   - Make sure the comment still matches the fixes he ticked. If it still asks the author for a ticked fix (the fix's `ask` phrase), or says "I pushed" for a fix he left unticked, stop and ask him rather than editing his text.
3. **Fixes:** apply each ticked `fixes[].id` on the contributor's branch.
   - Use a worktree under the scratchpad, never the main checkout. The PR must have `maintainerCanModify` set.
   - Prefer merging main to rebasing, so you never force-push over a contributor's history.
   - Regenerate generated files with their build scripts, and run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` before pushing.
   - The commit message ends with the session's Co-Authored-By line.
   - A fix that targets main, like `builder-main`, becomes its own branch and PR off main.
4. **Review:** `event` APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT → `gh pr review <n> --approve|--request-changes|--comment --body-file <file>`. `NONE` → post nothing.
   - The comment is Merill's text, edited on the desk. Post it word for word, then add the block the page shows under "Added below your comment": a blank line, `**Changes I pushed to your branch:**`, then `- <note>` for each ticked fix that isn't `internal`, in `fixes[]` order. Leave the block out if a fix wasn't pushed, and say so in `outcome`.
   - Do the steps in the order the card's "Claude will" box lists them: internal fixes, then the branch fixes, then the review, then the merge.
   - **Assignee:** when the PR now waits on its author (REQUEST_CHANGES, or a NONE/COMMENT on a PR whose changes are still requested), assign the author: `gh pr edit <n> --add-assignee <author>`. When you approve or merge, remove the author if they are assigned: `--remove-assignee <author>`.
5. **Merge:** only if `merge` is true and CI is green on the commit you just pushed. Use `gh pr merge <n> --merge`.
   - Never enable auto-merge. If CI is still running, leave the PR and say so.
6. **Record:** update `decisions/<n>` to `status: "done"` with `doneAt`, and `prs/<n>.outcome` with one line on what happened, including links or SHAs.
   - Pin each write to the version you read, with `if_version`.
7. **Report** in chat what was posted, pushed and merged, and anything you skipped and why.

## Data schema

`prs/<number>` is written by Claude:
- **Identity:** `number`, `title`, `author`, `url`, `headSha` (12 chars), `size` (`"+a/-d · n files"`).
- **State:** `merge` (`mergeable|conflicting|behind|blocked`), `ci` (`passing|failing|pending`), `ciNote`.
- **Verdict:** `verdict` (`ready|small-fix|changes|decision|merged|closed`), `order` (rank: ready first, then by complexity).
- **Review:** `reviewedAt` (ISO), `summary`, and `question`, used only when Merill must rule on something.
- **Findings:** `findings[]`, each `{sev: high|medium|low|nit, text, where}`.
- **Fixes:** `fixes[]`, each `{id, text, note, ask, internal, preselect}`. These are things we could do ourselves.
  - `text`: what we'll do, shown beside the checkbox.
  - `note`: the line added to the comment when it's ticked, in the past tense ("Added the missing trailing newline to `x.md`.").
  - `ask`: an exact phrase from the draft comment that asks the author for the same change. The page warns when the fix is ticked and the phrase is still in the comment.
  - `internal: true` for work that isn't on the author's branch (approving fork workflows, merging main before merge). It gets no `note` and isn't mentioned in the comment.
  - Write the draft comment so it reads right with the fixes unticked. The page adds the ticked fixes' notes.
- **Draft:** `event` (`APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT|NONE`) and `comment`, which is markdown for GitHub.
- **History:** `outcome`, a one-line log of the last action.

`decisions/<number>` is written by the page:
- **Review:** `comment`, `event`, `fixes[]` (ticked ids), `merge` (bool).
- **State:** `status` (`draft|queued|hold|done`), `prSha`, `decidedAt`, and `doneAt`, which Claude sets.

Inline text renders `` `code` `` and `**bold**`.

## Writing the comment

- Address the author with their real @login, and thank them once.
- Plain English, short bullets, and bold labels for the blocking items. No emoji, and no headings beyond bold.
- Say clearly what blocks the merge and what is optional.
- When CI fails because of main, tell them it isn't their fault and that we'll fix it.
- Never write "I pushed …" in the comment. The page adds pushed fixes from their `note`, so the comment matches what is ticked.

## Process notes

Merill's rulings go here as they come up.

- Skip contributors' draft PRs.
- Read the existing reviews before reviewing.
- A benchmark test that duplicates another suite's check is a shim.
- No "(Preview)" in test titles.
- Take `headSha` from `git rev-parse --short=12` or `gh`, never typed from memory. A wrong SHA looks like a moved PR.
- A PR that merged after he queued it can't be approved. Post the comment with `gh pr comment` and record that.
- Locally, `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` "skips the family when the module is not installed" fails because the module is installed on his Mac. Ignore it; every other failure blocks a push.
- Write large desk docs from a JSON file (`ArtifactData set` with `file_path`); long inline JSON can fail to parse.
- A contributor who pushes a change and then reverts it may reopen it as a new PR. Compare the two with `git patch-id`.
- Pushing to a contributor's branch dismisses the approvals already on the PR. Re-approve after the push, not before.
- Fork workflows can wait at `action_required` after we push. Approving them is an `internal` fix.
- When a PR moves after a decision was `done`, set its decision back to `draft` with the new draft, so it shows under Needs you.
- A PR waiting on its author is assigned to them, so the GitHub list shows whose move it is (ruling 2026-10-31).
